641\. Doc agent (2026-11-09): the human asked why `et-design.mjs` processes stay behind again and again. pid 1117702
(from 15:27) ran 3 h 25 min as an orphan: its parent `yarn et:design` was reparented to systemd, so the shell that
started it was gone, and the auto mode refused the builder's kill. The human had it killed. Cause: the wrapper
`tools/scripts/et-design.mjs` runs the cli with `spawnSync`, so it blocks, forwards no signal, and never sees that its
parent died; with no deadline (finding 640) it waits forever. Why no tool caught it: the orphan check of B282 covers
only e2e-check runs, not cli runs from an agent shell. Tool fix (with item 0, same cause as 640): the wrapper spawns
the cli async in its own process group, forwards SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP to that group, and ends the group when its
parent is gone (ppid changes); `design` refuses to start a second run of the same command while an older one lives and
names its pid.

As built (640/641): `tools/scripts/et-design.mjs` spawns the cli async, detached in its own process group unless stdin is
a terminal (a background group stops on SIGTTIN when `et design` reads stdin), forwards SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP, polls
`/proc/self/stat` every 1.5 s and ends the group when its parent changed, SIGKILL 5 s after SIGTERM. A lock per
checkout + argv in `$TMPDIR/et-design/locks` refuses a second identical run with the old pid; a dead pid's lock is taken
over. Deadlines from `.ethlete/design/.timings.jsonl` (2026-11-08): slowest normal `shot` 38 s (14 runs), `check` 560 s
(88 runs), so `shot` 5 min and `check` 20 min in `libs/cli/src/lib/design/run-deadline.ts`; the cli exits 124 and writes
`$TMPDIR/et-design/deadline/<cmd>-*.log` (last step, ended phases, last 200 output lines). The wrapper backstop (6 / 22
min) kills the group and writes `wrapper-*.log`. `ETHLETE_DESIGN_DEADLINE_MS` overrides both. Cause of the 55 min shot:
its timing line shows 374 cache misses and 3.3 M ms unphased after browser-start, no step named; one visible gap is
closed: a part draw (`page.evaluate` calls have no limit) now fails after 4x the load-scaled draw timeout and closes its
page. Specs: `tools/scripts/et-design.spec.mjs`, `run-deadline.spec.ts`, `warm-pages.spec.ts`, each bites with its
fix removed. Not verified: a real `shot` hitting the deadline in Chrome (a probe showed `process.exit` and SIGTERM both
end Playwright's Chrome).

644\. Builder (2026-11-09, item 0, 07596570b): the Studio e2e flakes ("no frame after 10 s", `/__design/stamp` at about
7 s on CI) come from the design server blocking its event loop while it answers `GET /__design/open-points`:
`openPointsAnswer` → `ruleProblemsOf` runs the Tailwind check with a blocking `execFileSync`, and `declaringFilesOf`
walks files synchronously, 6-10 s per run locally, 2-3× more on CI. Every other request waits behind it. Fix (item 0):
compute the open-points answer in a worker thread, like `merge-runner.ts`. Why no tool caught it: nothing keeps sync
child processes and long sync loops out of a request handler. Tool fix (backlog, per ADR 0235 at the cause): a heavy
studio-api answer runs through one worker building block, and lint forbids `execFileSync`/`spawnSync` in code
reachable from studio-api handlers (same rule family as the git reader of 642); an event-loop lag assertion in the
server specs is only the fallback. First e2e speedup in the same commit: 169.8 s → 146.3 s (one run).

As built (639/644): `GET /__design/open-points` runs in one long-lived worker (`system/open-points-runner.ts`,
`open-points-worker.ts`) with its own open-points cache; a draw stays on the server thread and passes its findings in.
Measured on the studio product from dist: the loop stalled 2.1 s (cold, all parts), 2.0 s (one part) and 0.3 s (warm);
in the worker the longest loop gap is 7 ms. In the jiti worker of the specs the cache missed every read after its
first tracked run (jiti keeps the `fs` function a module first called), so `tracked-reads.ts` keeps its recorders
installed. `open-points-loop.spec.ts` bites with the old answer (1021 ms gap). The jiti worker starts in 4-7 s: 30 s
spec timeouts.

As built (647): the cause was `liveShotsOf` in `system-view/sketch-view.component.ts`. It only kept frames of near
cells (400px margin, cap 6), so a cell whose frame had painted but whose picture had not loaded yet lost its frame
when it scrolled out of the near band. On return it mounted a new frame and stayed empty until that frame painted.
Under load the low-priority `__design/shot` pictures arrive late, so the cells rely on their frames, and the scroll
back up hit them (the `up1 a product` rows). Fix: a painted cell without a loaded picture stays live, near or not,
outside the cap, until its picture loads. The cap still governs the near cells. Reproduction: CPU load alone (8-10
parallel runs plus 24-56 busy loops, or CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` 4x/8x) never reproduced it. Holding the
picture responses (a context route that delays `__design/shot` by 60 s) reproduces it deterministically: 6/6 fail
before (`up1+30 current product [pic:pending]`), 6/6 pass after (8/8 overall, plus 5/6 with one start-up timeout
while two page groups ran alongside). Verified: the case alone and with `--hold-listings 14000`, `--page Large` 32/32
and `--page Sketches` 26/26 (one Large run under extra load failed the listing-refresh 150px case, which passed 3/3
alone on both builds and in a quiet rerun), the sketch-view spec (a new `liveShotsOf` spec fails on the old code),
tsc, eslint. Not fixed: the other half of the failures (`down7+300 a section (iframe: no frame)`, also `no context`)
is a probe race in the case, not an empty cell. With pictures delayed 3 s, a MutationObserver and a probe-time read
show that the census saw the frame with the picture pending, then the picture loaded, the frame was swapped out, and
the probe hit a detached iframe; at that moment the cell showed its loaded picture (`img true/1440/1, iframe none`).
That race fails about 1/4 runs before and about 7/16 after the fix (more live frames swap out when pictures land).
It needs a case fix: re-census a cell whose probe says `no frame` or `no context`. Not verified: a full 8-worker
suite run. Why the design tools missed it: compare, verify and check read settled pictures and frames of one state.
None scrolls the sketch view, and none runs with late pictures, so a cell's empty time during a scroll is invisible
to them. Tool fix: the decided e2e load mode that the repeat gate runs. Generic CPU load is a poor base because it did
not reproduce. A better base is a load mode that delays the design server's slow paths (picture shots by several
seconds, frame loads by a smaller amount), as the delayed-shot route here does.

As built (647, part 1, ec946602e): `liveShotsOf` in `sketch-view.component.ts` kept frames only for near cells, so a
painted cell without a loaded picture lost its frame when it left the near band and stayed empty on return. Such a
cell now stays live until its picture loads; the spec bites. CPU pressure (56 busy loops, CDP throttle 8x) never
reproduced it; a 60 s delay on `__design/shot` did, 6/6 fail before, 8/8 pass after. The e2e case has a race of its
own: `probeCell` reads a frame that Studio removed after its picture loaded and reports "no frame" or "no context",
while the cell shows its picture. Doc agent decision (the test intent stays, so no question for the human): on those
two answers `probeCell` counts the cell again from a new census; an empty cell still fails, and the case must still
fail with the `liveShotsOf` fix reverted. The 647 load mode uses a delay on the design server's slow paths (pictures
by several seconds, frames by less), not CPU pressure; base: the subagent harness `/tmp/s647/zz-load-647.e2e.mjs`.

As built (647 part 2, in progress): `canvas.e2e.mjs` gets `--delay-pictures <ms>` (`STUDIO_E2E_DELAY_PICTURES`), a
route that delays every `__design/shot?` request: the 647 load mode, moved from the scratch harness. `probeCell`
counts a cell again from a new census when its probe gives `no frame` or `no context`, and judges it from that
census; a cell that is still empty fails. Verified: the scroll case with the fix and `--delay-pictures 60000` passes
3 of 3. Not verified yet: the bite proof (the `liveShotsOf` fix reverted, the same run must fail), the full 8-worker
suite, and the repeat gate with a delay run.

As built (647, part 2, 2b0227f8e): `canvas.e2e.mjs --delay-pictures <ms>` delays every `__design/shot?` request (the
load mode, moved from `/tmp/s647`); `probeCell` counts a cell again from a new census on "no frame" or "no context".
With the fix and a 60 s delay the scroll case passes 3/3. Open: the bite proof, the full suite, push:suite. Doc agent

As built (639/0237, check cache): the sketch check worker keeps each `rules` and `sketches` result per kind, target
and product (`cachedCheckOf`, `sketch/sketch-check-cache.ts`) with the stat and folder listing of every file the run
read (`trackedRun`, the open-points cache pattern); any changed print runs the check again. Not covered by the prints:

other sessions), all passed. A diagnostic run saw 582 hits and 57 misses; 36 misses are the first check of a fresh

`ReferenceError: __DELAY__ is not defined` in `tools/scripts/studio-e2e-repeat.mjs`. `push-suite.mjs:18` imports

(`node <export>/tools/scripts/push-suite.mjs`), so the gate is the committed gate; a spec checks that a dirty
`tools/scripts` file does not change the run. Until then: run push-suite only with a clean `tools/scripts`.

the outer removes the export. `studio-e2e-repeat` and `stale-design-servers` load by dynamic `import()` in the inner
run, so the outer loads no sibling script. Spec: `reexecCommand` plan, and no static sibling import in the source

As built (667 c, shared shot store): the design server's shot store moved from `shots-<sha1 of the checkout path>` to
one `part-shots` folder under the work root, so every checkout that shares a `node_modules` (every e2e worker) shares
it. The read-files fingerprint is the one the store already had: the content hash of every file a picture was drawn
from, plus the scope string. Files and paths inside the checkout are now stored relative to it, so the same inputs in
another checkout give the same fingerprint. A key keeps up to 4 variants, one per fingerprint, so a checkout with a
changed file gets its own picture and never takes the other's; `drop` drops only the variant this server used. The
server snapshot folder (`server-<pid>`) was a stored input under its real path, which the old filter missed through
the e2e checkout's `node_modules` symlink; it is filtered by both paths now. The vite `cacheDir` stays per checkout:
vite's config hash includes `root` and `resolve` (`getConfigHash`), and `resolve.alias` holds the checkout's paths, so
a shared folder would be rewritten by each checkout. The draw ledger counts `drawnTotal` (`/__design/queue`), and each
e2e worker prints its draws in the `ready` line and after each case.

per case in both runs. New, warm run: 12 in setup, 0 in every case. Cause: the path-keyed store. The 12 left are

all of them keys whose inputs read `zoom-chip.ts`; no other key drew. Unit spec: same files in two checkouts give one
entry and a hit; a changed file misses only that picture and keeps the other checkout's.

11.6-11.9 s, 22 draws each; HEAD with `--hold-listings 14000` 7/7, 122.1 s, fixtures 36.2-37.7 s, warmUp 11.3-12.3 s.

93.4 s, fixtures 33.2-34.6 s, warmUp 11.3-11.6 s, 0 draws in 5 of 7 cases. Load was 18 to 27 in these runs, so the
times are noisy. Not solved: workers that start at the same time with a cold store still each draw the same shots, as

As built (671/B465, finding 672): the cause was the sketch view, not the case's probe. `sketchRowsOf` puts the
revision into the frame address of every variant row, so a sketch edit gives each cell of row `a` a new address. The
same `<iframe>` got the new `src`, `FramePaintedDirective` emitted `false` at once, and the cell hid its frame. A cell
whose picture had loaded fell back to it; a cell shown only by its painted frame, picture not loaded yet (late pictures
under load), was empty until the new frame painted, about 80 animation frames (1.3 s) per cell. Fix
(`sketch-view.component.ts`): `paintedFrames` keeps each painted frame's address, and `frameSrcs` renders the frames
with `@for ... track src`, so the painted frame stays mounted and shown under the new one until that one paints. The
case also measured the wrong cells: it took its picture set as soon as any cell showed, and with late pictures only the
`current` row (unchanged by the edit) had painted, so it passed without testing an edited cell. It now waits for a
cell of variant `a`. The hold run held the listings 14 s, past the case's 10 s window, so the edit never reached the
page there; the case opts out of the listing hold (`holdListings: false`, the runner's per-case flag, listed as
`[listings not held]`), so the gate's hold run tests it with pictures delayed 60 s, and `studio-e2e-repeat.spec.mjs`
checks that. Bite: `--delay-pictures 60000` fails 3/3 on the old component (all three row-`a` cells lost, the
reported message) and passes 3/3 with the fix (0 empty animation frames); with the hold-run arguments 1/1 fail before,
1/1 pass after; plain runs pass 2/2 with the fix; a new sketch-view spec fails on the old component. Load 4.8 to 8.4 throughout. Why no gate caught it:
the case only bit when a visible variant cell had a painted frame and no loaded picture, which needs late pictures,
and the one run with late pictures held the listings past the case's window. Not verified: a full suite or push:suite
run.

714\. Builder (2026-11-10, day shift, CI 42818705706 on 0a4e96f88): Unit tests red, only query
`src/scenarios/auth-features.scenario.spec.ts:403` "reports the expiry from a custom expiration claim": `expected 18000

boundary flake where the expiry read sees a clock that did not advance on the fake clock (off by one between `settle`
and the expiry tick); last commits there 3bf4f45db, ab8d48ca2. The fresh builder fixes it first (ADR 0230). Tool gap:

As built (714, builder subagent). Cause: `useScenario` started the fake clock at the real wall time, so the millisecond
fraction was random; tokens floor `exp`/`iat`/`eat` to whole seconds. At a .999 start the custom-claim test reads
exactly 18000 (bite: the CI message, reproduced with `SCENARIO_CLOCK_FRACTION=999`), and at a .000 start 9 other auth
tests failed, each ticking to exactly the instant the refresh fires while its response lands 1 ms later (8 tests), or to
1 ms before the next expiry check (the expiration warning). No lib bug. Fix: the harness pins the clock at
2100-01-01T00:00:00.500Z (`scenarioStartMs()`, far future because jsdom's cookie jar expires cookies against the real
clock), `SCENARIO_CLOCK_FRACTION=0|999` moves it to a second edge, the tests tick past the boundary they mean, the
custom-claim test asserts `>= 18000` (the floor a .999 mint reaches), and the persistence seeds read the pinned start
instead of the real clock. `src/scenarios` passes at .500, .000 and .999. Tool gap: CI runs only the default pin; a CI
step for the two edge runs is proposed, not built.

714 Cause (builder bite): the query scenario harness (`libs/query/src/scenarios/harness/scenario.ts:655`) fakes `Date`

about 1 in 1000 runs today. Fix in progress: the harness pins one start instant; each of the 11 is sorted into timing in
the spec or a real lib boundary bug (lib bug: fix plus scenario). Tool fix: the pinned start makes a boundary fail on
every run; the doc agent adds that the harness also runs the suite at the two edge fractions (`.000`, `.999`) once,
so a boundary bug cannot hide behind the one pinned value.

`useScenarioClock()`); a future date because jsdom's cookie jar expires cookies against the real clock.
`SCENARIO_CLOCK_FRACTION=0|999` moves the start to an edge. Causes of the 11 (traced): 8 refresh scenarios fired exactly
at the end of `s.tick(N)` at `.000` with the response 1 ms later (tick 1 ms further); the expiration-warning check
samples once a second (settle 15000); 2 maxAge scenarios seeded with real `Date.now()` (now `scenarioStartMs()`). No lib
bug. The 714 assert is `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(18000)`: at `.999` the floored `eat` loses 999 ms, so 18000 is the exact

passed; `spec:stress` 4/4. Decided (doc agent, ADR 0240 "as fast as possible"): CI runs the two edge fractions as
parallel jobs, so the wall time of the query step does not grow.

780\. Mac builder (2026-11-11, night, 770 81980de90): the Mac push was refused four times tonight because origin moved
while its push:suite ran (last: 14 commits, then a full rerun with the 29 min repeat step). Cause (measured in the push
log): both builders push to `next`; every Linux range touched `libs/cli` or `tools/`, so the 770 step reuse never
applies. Lesson: two pushers with half-hour gates need a slot, not luck. Decided by the doc agent (tool internal, the
Mac builder's recommendation, with one change): a builder that starts push:suite for a push to `next` claims a push slot
for its run time; the other builder commits but holds its push until the slot ends. The `agent-sessions claim` store is
per checkout and does not reach the other machine, so the slot lives on origin (for example a ref with holder and
expiry), has an expiry so a dead run cannot hold it, and is released when the push ends or the suite fails. A spec
bites with two claimers. Tool fix (night backlog, Mac builder, after its push). Built bc219f75d (note 28e202402): ref
`refs/push-slot/next` on origin, a parentless commit whose message holds the holder (`ETHLETE_BUILDER`, else the
hostname), the sha and a 60 min expiry; claim and release with `--force-with-lease` on the read slot; free when absent,
expired, or its sha is in origin/next; released on a blocked verdict or SIGINT/TERM/HUP. Spec bites with plain
`--force`. Verified live: GitHub accepts the ref. Not verified: a two-machine run, clock skew, signal release.

As built (780, `bc219f75d`): `tools/scripts/push-slot.mjs` keeps a push slot on origin at `refs/push-slot/next`. It is a commit with no parent whose message holds the holder (`ETHLETE_BUILDER`, else the hostname), the sha and an expiry 60 min out: 40 min of suite plus up to 10 min of load wait. Claim and release lease on the slot commit they read (`--force-with-lease`), so of two claimers exactly one wins. The slot is free when it is absent, expired, or its sha has reached `origin/next`, so the push itself releases it. `push:suite` claims at the start and stops with a blocked verdict naming the holder and expiry; it releases on a failed verdict or signal. `.husky/pre-push` refuses a push of `next` while another holder has a live slot. Verified: `push-slot.spec.mjs` (6 cases, bare origin and two clones; it bites when the lease is replaced by `--force`), spec:stress 4/4, `push-suite.spec.mjs` green, and a manual blocked run. Not verified: GitHub accepting the custom ref, a real two-machine run, clock skew. Rule for the other builder: when `push:suite` says the slot is held, keep committing and rerun it after the holder's push lands or the slot expires (`yarn push:slot status`); `yarn push:slot release` frees a dead run's slot.

As built (786, Mac builder): `tools/scripts/heavy-run-lock.mjs` holds one lock file per machine

is taken over; a child of a holder (env `ETHLETE_HEAVY_RUN_HELD`) takes none. The lock ends with the suite (ok or
blocked) and on process exit. Specs: `heavy-run-lock.spec.mjs`, two real runner processes; the second stops with
`heavy run lock held by push-suite (pid ...)`. Bite: without the holder check it fails. Not verified: a live
push:suite next to a spec:stress; a subagent run in another checkout of the same machine (same tmpdir, so covered).

As built (Linux builder, 745): `startCommandOf(base)` (stamp.ts) gives `DE_PORT=<port of base> et design`. The
`serve-state` "nothing answers" hint, its terminal restart line and the stamp `NO SERVER` line name it instead of

(`terminalPortLine`, serve.ts) in place of "not started by Studio, so it listens on a free port". Bite: with
`startCommandOf` back to `et design`, 2 of 4 serve-state cases fail; with the change 4/4, the `terminalPortLine` case
passes, cli typecheck passes. Not verified: a real terminal `et design` run that shows the new line.

As built (Linux builder, 736+737): `sketchHoldingOf` (shot-command.ts) resolves `<part>@<name>` to that exact sketch.
A bare `<part>` draws the unnamed sketch on the part (the rule `findSketch` already has), else the only sketch on it;
with several named sketches it refuses and names the `<part>@<name>` targets. A named shot writes its own sheet file
(`<product>-<layer>-<name>.<sketch>.png`). An `--at` shot records a view on the live sketch, at the content of the
commit, so it counts while the live content equals that commit. The viewed record now holds the content hash, the shot
file and its sha256. `recordShotViewed` takes the shot file and records nothing when it cannot read it. The design
server writes the shot it hands out to `viewed-shots/<sketch>-<variant>.png` and records that. `sketch ready` refuses
when the record's shot file is gone or drawn over. A record from before (a bare content hash) counts as not viewed,
with "its viewed record predates shot hashes, so view the shot again". Bite: with `sketchHoldingOf` back to the first
holder, 3 cases fail ("draws the sketch a <part>@<name> shot names, not the first one on the part", "refuses a bare
part and names the <part>@<name> targets, but draws the unnamed sketch of a bare part", "refuses a bare shot of a part
with two named sketches before it draws"). With the check back to content only, "refuses ready on a viewed record
without a shot the CLI drew of the current content" fails: a direct `recordShotViewed` without a drawn shot readied the
sketch. With the fix, the touched specs pass and cli typecheck passes. Not verified: a real `design shot
<part>@<name> --variants` run in a browser, and a real `--at` shot of a named sketch.

As built (Linux builder, 766 item 2, archive rule): `archive-findings.mjs` also moves a finding of any age when STATUS.md

deletes done rows, so no finding is ever done, and the age rule (over 5 days) held back every finding from 11-05 on.
First run moved 22 findings (641-715), plan 440205 to about 364000 chars. Bite: the new spec case fails with the old age

B416 phase 3 = S4 (in progress, then as built in the `perf(cli)` commit that adds this note, c0 subagent, 2026-11-06):
compare keeps its pictures on disk under `node_modules/.design-explore/compare-{design,app}-shots-<hash>`. A design
picture uses the design server's shot store (`server.shotStore`): its key is the frame (part, state, preset, width, bare,
emptySlots, checker, theme), it is valid while every file it was drawn from is unchanged (part source, embedded parts and
kit, styles, tokens, config), and the salt is the cli build and the Playwright version; the store now keeps the frame's
text ambient. An app picture's key is the sha256 of the cli build, the Playwright version, the hash of every built
harness file, the harness path and query (part, state, props, layout) and every other shot option (size, width,
forced, opened control and its markup, room, panes, frozen, ambient, prop check). No app cache for `--url`. A hit skips
the shot and counts in `design timings`; the action check reuses the design store. Numbers (studio, read-only, resident
off): pages/sketches cold 21.1 s, warm 8.0 s (91 hits, 0 misses; compare-states 0.7 s, compare-actions 3.9 s, ~3 s
process start); every design picture invalidated 14.4 s, the built app invalidated 13.6 s; pages/start 2.7 s cold, 1.8 s
warm. Floor after an edit: 30 design or app shots 6-7 s; compare-actions 3.5-3.9 s, mostly `actions-state` per state
(matrix states ~1.9 s).

inside `#studio-menu-surface`), which the closed menu marks `hidden`; the same false count hit studio-menu's own
four closed states. The counter now walks the tag tree and skips any mock inside a `hidden` element. A capped pane
wait fails the state again ("the design draws N overlay pane(s), the app opened M ..."); the note path is gone. No
time gained: the wrong count never cost the 1 s cap, because the wait already exits early once the open panes settle
with no new one (settle 0.05-0.18 s per shot before and after). pages/sketches warm 6.7 s, app pictures dropped

is 30 shots 4 at once (5.6 s, ~0.6 s of a wide shot is queue wait), compare-actions 2.9 s and ~3 s process start.
B416 compare-actions (as built in the `perf(cli)` commit that adds this note, c0 subagent, 2026-11-06): the 30 s
timeouts on elements/studio-menu and components/shell-project-switch were `readRingProbe` waiting Playwright's default
30 s for a menu item its own click had removed; it now answers `null` at once for a gone element, waits at most 1 s

Open-points key and revision guard (as built in the commit that adds this note, subagent, 2026-11-06). Part 1:

fs spy on every non-write `*Sync` function asserts the acme rules open nothing the tracker missed; guard spec (finding

each give a fresh result. Repeat call on the main checkout: icons 12, logo 11, shell-main 38 ms (before 14-18, 14-16,
~42). Part 2: the shooter hashes each kept picture; a changed hash for a key that no `forget` or announced `clear`
dropped calls `changed`, and the server sends a `parts` event with the next revision. Bug fixed on the way: a flows
change cleared the shots without a `parts` event. canvas e2e `a part edited on disk while away shows its new picture on
return`: passes (12/12 pictures changed), fails with Studio's part revision held constant. Details:
`.claude/handoffs/agent-results/open-points-key-revision-guard.md`.

Open-points read-tracked key and revision guard (as built in 934616670, c0, 2026-11-06): `tracked-reads.ts` wraps the
sync fs calls (read, exists, stat, readdir/opendir) during the rule run; a hit needs the same product JSON and every

holds in memory (no rule uses them; not proven).

537\. c0 (2026-11-06), S7b-2 real-edit run: the S7b-1 render cache and the new completeness cache never verified
anything. Node re-fetched the recorded URLs on 127.0.0.1 while Vite listened on ::1, so every input hash was null
(14 814 render, 5 612 completeness entries), and null == null counted as unchanged: every entry always hit. A scratch
edit of zoom-chip ('Fit' -> 'Fitting') redrew nothing. SDK renders (`POST /__design/render`) were re-fetched as GET and
always got the same 405, so SDK markup was never in the key. The S7b-1 numbers (205 s warm) and the first S7b-2
numbers (48.4 s warm) are invalid. Why no tool caught it: every cache spec used a fake server with a fetchable URL, none
ran against a real Vite listen address, no spec required non-null input hashes for a hit, and S7b-1 reported its
numbers before a real-edit run (rule of finding 519). Tool fix: built in 52c079983 (fetch the server's own listen
address, a null hash never counts as unchanged, render requests re-posted with their recorded body, specs for each).
Doc agent adds: the cache writes no entry unless every input hash is non-null; `design timings` shows the null-hash
count per run and flags any above 0; and a cache slice reports no numbers and is not done until a real edit in a
scratch worktree has redrawn exactly the edited part and its embedders.

599\. Builder (2026-11-08, CI at 334243fe4): `merge.spec` stall 277 ms over a 91 ms bound, Linux only. Cause real:
libuv `fork()` on the server thread blocks in proportion to the RSS (29-173 ms per spawn at 3.8 GB), and a merge
spawns git up to 5 times; macOS uses `posix_spawn` and hides the cost, so every local run was green. Fixed in b85f8fd40
(git calls run in the merge worker). Tool fix (technical, built in b85f8fd40): a spec asserts that the server thread
makes no `child_process` call, so the rule holds on every OS, not only where a stall shows. Built in b85f8fd40.

697\. Doc agent (2026-11-10, day shift, first `restart --process`, 3cfdb35d0): the typed `/exit` opened the Claude
Code dialog "Background work is running ... The following will stop when you exit: shell · gh run watch 42796254724"
with the choices exit and stop tasks, move to background and exit, stay. The restart waited on it until someone
answered (screenshot from the human). The new process then ran in a new tmux session `claude-3@ethlete-sdk`; the old
`claude@ethlete-sdk` was gone, so a check by session name fails. Cause (measured by the builder): the respawn runs `$SHELL -lic "claude <prompt>"`; in the login shell `claude` is the shell-install function, which calls `agent-sessions run`; with `$TMUX` set, `run` picks a free session name (claude-3), switches to it and exits, so the old pane dies and its session closes. Side defect: `run` stores the prompt in `@ethlete_command`, so the next `restart --process` types the stale `/handoff resume` first. Fix part: respawn with `command claude` (no shell function) and store only the base command. Tool fix: `restart --process` stops the background work of the session first (or
answers the dialog with "exit and stop tasks", since the handoff names the work), the handoff names each stopped
background job so the new process starts it again (here the CI watch), and the new process keeps the old tmux session
name. Bite: a session with a running background shell restarts with `--process` without a human, in the same tmux
session, and the new process resumes the watch.

As built (697): the respawn command starts with `command` (after any `VAR=value` prefix), so the shell function does
not run and the pane keeps its session. `run` stores the command without the trailing prompt (a last word that is not
a flag and not the value of a flag, or the words after `--`). After `/exit`, the restart reads the pane; on "will stop
when you exit" it moves the cursor to "exit and stop tasks", presses Enter, and writes the listed jobs to
`restart.log` and a mailbox notice. The handoff skill says to name each background job before `--process`. Verified:
three new specs (respawn bypasses a shell function, `run` stores no prompt, the dialog is answered), each fails with its
part reverted. Not verified: live bite with a real Claude session and the real dialog text and cursor.

435\. Tom (2026-11-04, screenshot after merge aa8c96889): every frame, the sample too, shows the Vite overlay

Tom guessed the parallel Studio build; it is not. Cause (builder, code read): the listing has no sketch any more, but
the frames still request the merged sketch. The server resolves imports of a module with `design-sketch=` through
`drawnOf` (`libs/cli/src/lib/design/system/system-modules.ts:94`); for a gone sketch it returns null and caches the
miss, so `@system/...` has no resolution. The sketch query spreads to product files, so every frame breaks. Probable,
not proved: Tom's view still held the sketch frames, and Vite HMR reloaded them with their old URLs after the merge.
Why no tool caught it: no spec or e2e requests a frame of a sketch after its merge or discard; the merge e2e ends at
the merge result. Tool fix (B367): (a) `drawnOf` resolves a gone sketch to the product, does not cache the miss, and
the frame shows a plain note instead of a Vite error; a spec. (b) Studio: when the open sketch drops from the
listing, the sketch view leaves it and drops the old frames; an e2e merges a fixture sketch with its view open and
asserts no error overlay and that the view leaves.

sketch.

skips parts without an `implements` link; `check --part` prints why it wrote no record.

record on the part's own check (open points, rules, slow results incl. COMPARE, actions) only; an embedded part that is
not build-ready keeps the host from build-ready (`design task`), not from its record, so `task --verify` (compare +
actions + implemented record) runs once the part's own check passes. `partActionFailuresOf` (`actions-command.ts`)
skips a part without an `implements` link with one line `actions <part>: skipped - no implements link, nothing to
click` (printed by `check --part`). `check --part` prints why it wrote no record (`NO RECORD <product> <part>:
<kind>: <text> (+n more)` or `the actions did not run`). A full check now also records unlinked parts whose own check
passes (`READY` lists them). Verified: specs with bite in `part-build-ready.spec.ts`, `part-ready.spec.ts` and
`check-system.spec.ts`.
Built in 708a440fb.

**Doc-agent decision under Q160 - multi-part verify, as built (2026-11-06):** `task <part> [<part>...] --product <p>
--verify <rev>` verifies one commit as one task over several parts. The allowed files are the union of the named parts'
allowed files. Files under `plans/`, `apps/ethlete-studio/docs/`, `.changeset/` and `apps/docs/components/` never count
as implementation files: they are skipped with one line (`notImplementationFilesOf` in `part-task.ts`), also for a
single part. Any other file outside the union is refused and named. Each part runs its own compare and actions check;
a part is recorded only when every named part passed, each with its own implemented hash. A refused verify names the
other linked parts whose allowed files hold the refused files: `verify together: et design task a b c --product <p>
--verify <rev>` (`ownerPartsOf`). Several parts without `--verify` exit 2 with a usage message. Verified: specs with
bite in `part-task.spec.ts` (union, foreign file, skipped plan/docs/changeset files, red compare on one part records
nothing, the hint, no `--verify`). Not verified: the real verify of ff698951f.

(`frame-revisions.ts`) moved only on a server `parts` event, but two paths swapped a picture without one: a flows change

stable URL, the 1 h cache and `ShotBoard.hold`, the old picture stayed. Why no tool caught it: no spec tied a store
write to Studio's revision; before frame A every switch fetched the picture again and hid the gap. Tool fix (done in
934616670): the shooter hashes every kept picture per key, and a changed hash that no announced redraw dropped calls
`changed(part)` (revision bump + `parts` event); `clear` requires `{announced}`. Guards: shot.spec and shot-store.spec
(flows change then a changed picture sends a `parts` revision; fails if the flows path claims announced) and the e2e
"a part edited on disk while away shows its new picture on return" (12/12 new pictures; fails with the revision held).
Lesson: a cache that makes a page faster also hides a missing invalidation, so every cache slice adds an
edit-while-away e2e before it is called done.

picture cache, parallel lanes) accepted. A check in the resident must not push a compare past its 10 s target: the

a risk (fonts, frame assets, dist CSS, generated Tailwind output, config, capabilities, merged and pictures JSON) gets
its own edit-between-runs case (rule of 531).

A waiting compare runs between two parts of a running check (yield points in auto-accept, inspect groups and completeness; a jumped compare reuses the check's lib-build read and never restarts the warm server), and `design timings` flags a run with over 10 % (and at least 1 s) unphased time as UNEXPLAINED. S7b-1 as built (df132a653, 2026-11-06): `design check` caches the render issues of each part group (product, part, sketch) on disk (`render-issues` under the checkout's vite cache, 64 MB LRU, `writeCacheEntry` so nothing is written after an abort). The key is the group's frame descriptors (computed fresh from the SSR load each run, so config, presets, states, skips and namespaces are in it), the render-inspect code hash with the frame assets (`renderInspectCodeOf`) and the Playwright version; the entry keeps every request the browser context made while drawing the group (url, accept header) with a hash of what the server answered, and is reused only while each of those urls answers the same when Node fetches it again (each url once per run, 30 s timeout). The drawing pages run with the browser cache off, so a module served from memory cache is still recorded. That covers part files, shared imports, tokens, the generated Tailwind output, fonts, frame.html and frame assets and the SDK dist CSS/JS without a hand-made fingerprint; merged.json, pictures.json and capabilities are neither served nor read by render inspect. The infra (`served-cache.ts`: `createServedHashes`, `createServedCache`, `servedHitOf`) is generic for S7b-2. Numbers (load ~3/32, sha df132a653 dirty only by the design json, resident): first run 309.2 s with render-inspect 95.1 s (cold cache), unchanged rerun 205.0 s with render-inspect 0.75 s; completeness 155.9 s is now the slowest phase. Verified: `render-cache-draw.spec.ts` drives the real `renderIssuesOf` on a fake WarmDraw (fake browser and page, real `inspect`), cold draws each frame once, warm 0, a part edit only that part, one case each for part file, shared import, CSS token, Tailwind output, font, frame asset, SDK dist CSS and JS, a changed state set, a no longer fetchable url, and config/capabilities/merged/pictures edits redrawing nothing; a broken `unchanged` fails 10 of 15. writes (`sketches/*.edit` folders, merged/ready/pictures.json) - redraws everything. The main tree only looked warm

specs edit one input of a fake part graph, none loads the real global virtual modules, and nothing runs the check twice

check, then an unchanged rerun on a fresh worktree must redraw 0 parts - and the cache key of a part holds only the
registry slice it reads, never a module that a check run rewrites. Done when the zoom-chip edit redraws exactly
zoom-chip, canvas-viewport, pages/sketches, flows, system, merge and inbox, also after `yarn et:design stop`.

649\. Builder (2026-11-09, check cache): the Tailwind facts store was keyed only by stylesheet paths, so a theme change
gave stale answers; the bug existed before the cache. Why no tool caught it: each store builds its own cache key by
hand, and nothing checks that the key covers every input the store reads. Tool fix (backlog): every design CLI cache
takes its key from the shared fingerprint of the files the run read, never a hand-built key; a spec per store changes
each input once and expects a fresh answer.

As built (649): `readsCacheOf` in `system/tracked-reads.ts` is the shared store: the slot names the request, and an
entry lives while every file and folder listing the run read still prints the same (`trackedRun` now nests, so an inner
cached run no longer ends the outer run's recording). Moved onto it: the Tailwind facts store (`classFactsOf`: its
Tailwind child process reports the files it read, so a theme in a package counts), the SDK declarations store
(`sdkDeclarationsIn`, was mtime), the app files store (`appFilesOf`, was mtimes of reached files only, so a missing
template or a `tsconfig.base.json` change was stale) and `cachedCheckOf`. A spec per store changes each input once;
bite with the old keys: package theme (Tailwind), same-mtime edit (declarations, app files), appearing template and
tsconfig path (app files) fail; the nesting spec fails without the outer chain. Remaining stores, not checked: the
disk and async caches `action-cache`, `compare-cache`, `harness-build-cache`, `part-picture-cache`, `pixel-cache`,
`served-cache`, `generated-stylesheets`, `shot-store`, `vite-cache`, `sketch/unchanged-states`, `link-free`
`earlierFields`, `slow-checks` `bases`; `trackedRun` is synchronous, so they need an async fingerprint first. Not
verified: a Tailwind `@plugin` or `@config` JS module the child loads through ESM `import` is not recorded, and no
`design check` ran on a real product.

650\. Builder (2026-11-09, ADR 0237): the 3 measured e2e runs ran at a load average of 39-51 from other sessions, so
the times cannot show if the 90 s goal is met. Why no tool caught it: the e2e timing report has no load figure, so a
noisy measurement looks like a clean one. Tool fix (backlog, with ADR 0208 run timings): every e2e timing report
prints the load average at start and end and marks a run above a load threshold as "noisy, not a measurement".
As built (Linux builder, 2026-11-11): `apps/ethlete-studio/e2e/run-load.mjs` `runLoadLineOf`; `canvas.e2e.mjs` prints
`load <start> at start, <end> at end on <cores> cores` after the budget line, with " - noisy, not a measurement" when
either one-minute load is above the core count (the threshold of the design timings, ADR 0208). Verified: `run-load.spec.mjs`
2/2, fails with the threshold broken; one live `yarn studio:e2e --case` run prints the line. Real case run (2026-11-11):
`--case 'a sketch merged while its view is open opens the part view of the target'` passed 1/1 in 24.6 s, exit 0, and
printed `load 0.7 at start, 1.7 at end on 32 cores`. A noisy live run is not verified.

B499 S1 as built (Linux builder, 2026-11-13): Cause (probe): the Studio e2e checkout (`prepareCheckout` in
`canvas.e2e.mjs`) links every top-level entry of the main checkout, `libs` and `dist` included, and Nx does not find
projects through a linked `libs` (in such a copy `nx show projects` lists none, `nx show project types` says "Could not
find project types"), so the stale rebuild with `cwd: target` failed for a lib the main checkout's source had made
stale. Fix: `rebuildStaleDist` runs `nx build` in the Nx workspace that owns the real path of the build folder (nearest
`nx.json` above it, else the target). Running in the owner is right for both: a real checkout owns its `dist`, and in
the e2e copy the linked `dist` and `libs` are the main checkout's, so skipping them would draw from an old build. The
build stays `spawnSync`: async breaks `shot-stale-dist.spec.ts`, which mocks `spawnSync` and lies outside the slice
paths; S2 or a later slice takes it. Bite: a stale-dist spec with a linked checkout, red on HEAD (nx cwd was the linked

B499 P6 as built (Linux builder, 2026-11-13): Cause (measured): cold `/__design/open-points?product=studio` took
11.4 s = 0.5 s product rules + 10.9 s rule runs over 18 variants of 8 ready Studio sketches (`sketchProblemsOf`), 8.5 s
of it CANONICAL-CLASS with a Tailwind child per variant. Fix: `prefetchClassFactsOf` puts the class facts of the product
and every fresh variant on disk in one Tailwind run (1.33 s); a class-facts cache write merges with the stored entry
(concurrent writers dropped each other's facts); one open-points worker per product, warmed at serve start
(`warmOpenPointsOf`, behind `ETHLETE_DESIGN_SLOW_CHECKS`) and ended when the serve's HTTP server closes
(`stopOpenPointsWorkers`); the fresh variants run in a sync worker pool (`system/sync-pool.ts`, min(4, cpus - 1)
workers, the open-points worker blocks on `Atomics.wait`; a failed pool falls back to the calling thread). The pool
starts before the prefetch, so its workers load meanwhile, and ends after each batch: an idle serve holds no pool
worker. P6 (`--only P6`, scratch copy, CLI built in it): before FAIL, open-points 11720 ms; after PASS twice,
open-points 506 / 556 ms, warm system 50 / 50 ms, worst main-thread block 0 / 0 ms (poll 19.8 / 6.7 s). RSS of the
serve process (all its worker threads; Chromium not counted) on the scratch copy, sampled every 10 s for 150 s: with the
pool peak 4.45 GB, idle after the poll 2.83-2.89 GB; same build with the pool off (`useVariantPool(0)`) peak 3.54 GB,
idle 2.59-2.66 GB, open-points 1782 ms. The pool's own peak (3 workers) is about 1.1 GB during the warm-up; the idle
gap of about 0.25 GB is heap the ended workers left to the allocator. Same thread count idle (106) with and without
the pool. The open-points answer with the pool is byte-identical to the one without (51 parts, fresh cache each).
Bite: `tailwind-facts-merge.spec.ts` red on HEAD (`p-other` lost), `sync-pool.spec.ts` red with a one-worker pool
(1616 ms > 1200 ms), `serve-workers.spec.ts` red without the close hook (2 live workers, not 0); vitest related
144 files green; spec:stress 4/4 each (the three new specs and `slow-run.spec.ts`, `--load 2`). Verified: P6 on Linux on a scratch copy, twice. Not verified: P6 in CI, the
Mac, the main checkout, a pool worker that dies mid-batch (only the stall timeout, 60 s, catches it).

ci-red 1113b as built (Linux builder, 2026-11-13): CI run 43362984133, Checks: `scratch-checkout.spec.mjs` left
`scratch-spec-*` in its spec TMPDIR, all 9 tests green. Cause (git-level probe, not reproduced at spec level): `git
commit` starts `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach` (GIT_TRACE, git 2.56); a repo made like `makeRepo` and
removed with `rmSync(force)` right after the commit stays in /tmp with its `.git` (no error thrown) in 2/200 and 3/400
runs under 32 busy loops, and 0/400 with `-c maintenance.auto=false`. Fix: the spec commits with
`maintenance.auto=false` and removes every temp dir in `t.after` instead of inline at the test end. Bite: the old spec
and the new one under 16 busy loops, 8 parallel loops each, own TMPDIR per run: 0/320 leaks both, so the spec-level
bite did not bite; the git-level probe is the bite. Verified: the spec green with the tmp-leak hook. Not verified: CI;
the orphan `sh`/`sleep` processes in the job end are not from this spec. Other specs that commit in a temp repo through
`gitEnv` may leak the same way.

the label `recordBuildReady` gives every record. Probes on `studio`: the serve alone, no CLI call, rewrote 2 entries
in 5 minutes; an in-process `--part pages/system` check (`ETHLETE_DESIGN_RESIDENT=0`) wrote nothing, the 8 entries
changed in its window all carry the serve's pid and none is `pages/system`; the same check through the serve-hosted
resident left `git status .ethlete/design` empty. The serve is out of P5's scope: the P5 note and the docs ("`et design
ready` and the design server write the record") keep its writes, so its behaviour is unchanged. Fix (a defect P5
caused, ADR 0280): `withStampsInMemory` held its map in a module global, so in the serve process a serve-hosted check
swallowed the slow runner's writes and showed it the check's own records, and of two overlapping runs the later one
wrote to disk once the earlier ended; the map now lives in an `AsyncLocalStorage` scoped to the run. The stale "as
`design check` does" in slow-run.ts and record-settled.ts is gone. Bite: `stamp-files.spec.ts` 2 of 3 red on the old
code (server write during a check, run ending after an earlier one), 3 of 3 green after. Not verified: a full-product
check through the serve with pid attribution, the fix live in the serve (its dist build predates it); the serve's
records still read `"by": "et design check"`, which is why the probe looked like a check write (open point, serve
scope).

B501 proof (ADR 0280, recorded 2026-11-13 by the doc agent from the builder's proposal). Baseline: 36 uncommitted ready.json records, 34 written by the idle
serve (pid probe); its Cause is in S1 as built.

- P1 an idle serve leaves tracked files alone: scratch checkout, slow cache deleted, `yarn design` for 3 min, then
  `git status .ethlete/design` is empty.
- P2 only a named user action writes ready.json, merged.json or a sketch.json decision: a spec runs serve, check (with
  the legacy upgrade) and status, and every file stays byte-equal.
- P3 atomic steps: a spec kills merge, ready or pick at each step boundary, and the tree holds either the old or the new
  state.
- P4 uncommitted state is visible: `design status` and Studio name uncommitted ready marks and leftover or untracked
  sketch folders.
- P5 no false withdrawal: regenerated or reformatted files and a shared-copy base change keep a ready mark; only a
  variant edit takes it back, and the withdrawal is reported. A picked sketch refuses edits without `--reopen`.
- P6 generated files: every generated tsconfig passes Prettier (today 4 of 51 fail: sdk, studio, studio-lab, root),
  FORMAT skips gitignored files, and the tsconfigs point only at the installed CLI.
- P7 `design task` works once the part record exists, or names the blocker; every record has `cmd` in {check, ready,
  serve}.

Slices: S1 serve writes nothing tracked (468 rest, 981, the idle-serve line, task refusal); S2 atomic writer and a
per-product lock; S3 transactional merge, discard and rebase (416 434 469 590 574 889, the port Suspect); S4 ready-mark
lifecycle (551, all-states a, edit without `--reopen`); S5 visibility (568 729 919); S6 generated files (707 755 756).
Condition (ADR 0281): the S2 lock names what it removes. 755(b) (shot cache through the node_modules realpath, scratch
isolation) moves to B503.

828\. Large iframe flake (Mac builder, 2026-11-11; numbered 815 on the Mac, renumbered at the merge): "a variant equal to Aktuell keeps its iframes across a quick and a full listing" failed once at `--workers 5`, load 31.7 to 55, with "folded false; collapsed: iframe/row adds 2 removes 22". Cause: the case waited a fixed 60 s for the fold after its setup write, then measured anyway; under load the setup's full listing took longer, so the first fold of variant b (row b and the folded states leave the DOM, the `hidden` frames enter) landed inside the measured "collapsed" window. It also counted a listing at `response`, which `sendHeldJson` sends after the first 15 s keep-alive, before the body. The product drops no iframe. Fix (test only): the setup uses the measured phases' `refresh`, a listing counts on `requestfinished` after the write, deadline 2 x `FULL_COMPARE_MS`. Bite: `--hold-listings 25000` failed before with the same "folded false, adds 2 removes 22" (setup full listing cancelled by the 60 s write, fold at 113 s in the collapsed window) and passes after.

releasing and re-acquiring while B waits gives the slot to B; without the fix A wins. Queue: Mac builder, after 845.

### Build-ready decisions (2026-11-03, A10 pulled forward)

Tom: the go system is not extended any more; A10 replaces it now.

1. Build-ready replaces go and acceptance. Tom's only approval is picking a sketch variant; an automatic merge
   only when no picture changes. Build-ready is computed: the ready mark holds at the current design hash, every
   embedded part is build-ready, no check problem is attributed to the part, and a small harness run renders every
   state without SDK errors (new runner; today SDK errors are only a side effect of compare/live).
2. No manual hold, no go withdrawal (B70 is moot): everything comes in through sketches that pass the checks.
3. Who builds (Tom: "a designer should not have components built ... our system breaks once it gets complex", the
   fifagg start page as the example): by content, not by layer. A part is designer-buildable when it is
   presentational: inputs and outputs only, composed of SDK components and parts, no services, no data loading, no
   routing. A tool checks it on the part before the build and on the generated code after it; a failure makes it a
   developer part. Small fixes go through the same test.
4. A developer part's spec is the build-ready part (design files, all states, compare target); done is a green
   compare of app against design. No written brief from the designer.
5. No sprawl: an implementation embeds each embedded part through that part's implemented component and never
   copies its markup. The design half is INLINE-UI-IN-PAGE (B247); the app half reuses its detector.
6. Missing state (Tom: "if it gets that far, Studio failed, but it must not tear the developer out of his work -
   imagine the designer is on holiday"): the developer builds the missing state himself and may do anything,
   including CSS ("otherwise he is stuck again because the SDK lacks the component"). The state is marked as
   needing approval: Studio opens a sketch on the part with the developer's build as a variant (its screenshot),
   and compare passes that one state while the sketch is open. The designer picks it or adds a replacement
   variant; after the pick the code must match the design again. Studio's failure is caught earlier by a rule: a
   part that takes data or lists is build-ready only with declared loading, error and empty states.

Technical (doc agent): `design task` gates on build-ready and names the red checks; doneParts drops the go.hash term
(implemented.hash vs the current design hash); open points no-go/stale-go become not-build-ready; ACTION-UNDECLARED
is always on; go.actions/review carry moves to the ready mark; pictures.json kind go is rekeyed to ready; remove
go.json, accepted.json, the go-*.ts commands, the Studio give-go and accept buttons and endpoints, the git-safety
go rule, and the go docs, with a migration that deletes both files. Built as B249 (build-ready + removal), B250
(designer/developer split check), B251 (undesigned-state sketch + required data states). 7. User roles (Tom): none now. Designer part and developer part are properties of the part that tools check, not
of a person; the only human decision stays the sketch pick, with `by` as today. Roles and rights come with E8
(two designers on one design, multi-user sessions). 8. Solo case (Tom builds Studio as designer and developer, the builder agent does the developer work): the same
flow as a team. An undesigned state the builder renders becomes a sketch that Tom picks. No solo shortcut.

652, decided by the doc agent (2026-11-11, night; tool internal, the builder's recommendation; no ADR covers it, ADR 0009
was a one-time commit): step 1 moves only `pictures.json` (pure tool state: shot hashes) to a gitignored
`.ethlete/cache/<product>/pictures.json`; the tool reads the old path once as a fallback and never writes it again; one
commit removes the tracked files. `ready.json` and `sketch.json` stay tracked because they carry designer decisions (ready
marks, picks); the tool writes them only when a decision changes (no rewrite of an equal file, stable key order). Bite: a
design run with no decision leaves `git status` clean. Condition: before the move, the builder confirms that no reader on
another clone (the Mac, CI, a scratch copy, the push suite) needs the committed `pictures.json`; if one does, it reports
before it builds. Leave the uncommitted `merged.json` and `ready.json` edits in the tree untouched.
652 condition hit (Linux builder, code read + grep): `design check` (`accepted-pictures.ts` `baselineOf`) takes the
baseline of a part changed outside a sketch from the committed `pictures.json` record, else from the local part-picture
cache; on a clone with neither (the Mac, a fresh clone, a scratch copy) it opens an old/new edit sketch that waits for a
pick, where Linux auto-accepts an unchanged picture. No CI workflow, push suite or e2e reads the file. So today the file
is a shared baseline, not a cache. Decided by the doc agent (tool internal; it applies the existing auto-accept of an
unchanged picture to every clone): step 0 before the move: when baseline and cache miss, the tool draws the part at its
merged commit itself (the EDIT_OLD draw of `edit-sketch.ts` `refreshEditOld`) and compares on the same machine; only a
changed picture opens the edit sketch. If the old draw fails, ADR 0253 applies (sketch with only `new`). Bite: a fresh
clone with a direct edit that changes no picture auto-accepts and opens no edit sketch. Then step 1 (the move) as above.
Corrected (Linux builder, probe spec, 2026-11-11 night): the condition line above came from a code read and is wrong.
Today a clone with no record and an empty cache already auto-accepts an unchanged direct edit: `autoAcceptOf` opens a
temporary ready `<part>@edit` sketch, draws `old`, compares, and on no change discards it and records the merge (specs in
`accepted-pictures.spec.ts` cover both cases). So step 0 is already built, the committed `pictures.json` is a speed
cache, and step 1 goes ahead. Rest gap (Suspect, not measured): while the two draws run, the temporary edit sketch is on
disk, so a slow run can show "waits for your pick" for that time, and a killed run or `EDIT-OLD-NOT-DRAWN` leaves it
open. A sketch-free draw needs a sketches root through `DrawStates` and the warm server (large). Tool backlog, Linux,
after 793; first measure how long the sketch shows on the Mac.

B508 upload crop as built (2026-11-14): `et-dropzone` / `etDropzone` take `crop: DropzoneCropConfig | null` (`aspectRatio`, `maxWidth`, `maxHeight`, `type`, `quality`). Picked raster images wait in `pendingCrops()` until `confirmCrop(id, file)` / `cancelCrop(id)`; SVG and non-images upload directly. Cancel drops the image and keeps the current value. Headless `etDropzoneCrop` (+ `etDropzoneCropRect`, `etDropzoneCropHandle`) holds the rect in image pixels, aspect lock, clamping, pointer + keyboard (arrows move, shift + arrows resize) and the canvas `export()`; default `et-dropzone-crop`. No zoom. Verified: unit specs (math, export seam), component spec (crop → upload gets the cropped File, non-image skips, cancel), scenario, static Storybook Crop story in Playwright (800x400 PNG, drag corner + move + keys, uploaded preview 370x208 = the crop scaled, no console errors). Not verified: touch devices, Safari/Firefox, screen reader. Dropzone golden +5.1 KB gzip (crop component + `et-button`).

B508 upload file data as built (2026-11-14): `DropzoneExistingFileInfo` gains `mimeType` and `uploadedAt`; the upload configs (new + v2) gain `selectFileInfo(response)`, whose set fields override the picked file's name/size/type/preview. Entries gain `mimeType()`, `uploadedAt()` and `response()`. `errorMessage()` is now `null` when the body carried no message (no raw "Http failure response" text), and the list item shows the server message or the new `entryUploadFailed` label, plus size, date and thumbnail. Verified: directive + component specs, static Storybook ExistingFiles / ServerResponse stories in Playwright (see the commit's report). Not verified: single-file preview (shows no date or per-entry error), touch, screen reader. Dropzone golden +480 B gzip.

B508 upload compact row as built (2026-11-14): `et-dropzone` takes `layout: 'area' | 'row'` (`DROPZONE_LAYOUTS`, default `'area'`). `'row'` shrinks the drop area to one `--et-dropzone-row-height` (56px) row: empty it is the drop target with the prompt on one line; with a single file it renders the list item `et-dropzone-item` in place (thumbnail, name, size + date, thin progress bar, server error or `entryUploadFailed` label in place of size/date, retry or replace, remove), styles in a lazily mounted `et-dropzone-row-styles`. With `multiple` the row only shrinks the drop area. The single-file preview now shows the upload date and the per-entry error. Verified: component specs (row empty/filled, drop on trigger and on the row, error + retry, replace + remove, preview date + error), all 12 Dropzone stories in the Storybook vitest run, static Storybook CompactRow / CompactRowServerResponse in Playwright (56px in every state, `fail.png` shows the server error, ellipsis keeps the width). Not verified: the area preview's new date/error visually, touch, screen reader. Dropzone golden +1079 B gzip.

B508 standings expandable rows as built (2026-11-14): `ng-template[etStandingsRowDetail]` (`StandingsRowDetailDirective`, typed context `{ $implicit: row, renderRow, columnCount }`, self-registers on `StandingsDirective`, a second one throws `ET4402`) makes every `et-standings` row expandable. The headless directive owns the state: `expandedRows` (two-way `model` of row ids), `expandMode: 'single' | 'multiple'` (default `'multiple'`, the fifagg ask), `toggleRow(id)`, `isRowExpanded(id)`, and `isExpanded` / `detailId` on each render row. The component adds a trailing `data-column="expand"` column with a chevron `<button>` (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, label `rowDetailToggle(name)`, click does not bubble), and renders each row in its own `<tbody class="et-standings-row-group">` with the detail as a following `<tbody class="et-standings-detail">` holding the template's own `<tr>`s, so season sub-rows align to the team columns and collapse with them; the zone bar and tint continue down the detail. Not `et-collapse`: a height collapse cannot wrap table rows without breaking column alignment, so the detail fades and slides in/out via `animate.enter`/`animate.leave` (`--et-standings-expand-duration`, off under reduced motion). Whole-row click is not added. `et-standings-pick` is a separate component, so pick and expand never meet. Without the template the DOM is unchanged (one `<tbody>`, no column, no aria). Verified: component specs and three scenarios (aligned season rows with a working inner button, table click untouched, single vs multiple, two-way model, headless cards, duplicate template), Storybook vitest for all standings stories, static Storybook ExpandableRows in Playwright (fade runs, chevron turns, Enter/Space toggle, single mode closes the other row, `aria-controls` matches the detail id, season cells line up to the pixel at 900px, no overflow at 390px, no console errors besides the static build's missing Archivo fonts). Not verified: screen reader, touch, RTL edge on the detail. Golden delta: no standings entry; nothing moved by this change.

B508 match-card badge slot as built (2026-11-14): `etMatchCardBadge="<label>"` (headless part, in `MATCH_CARD_IMPORTS`) registers with the card; the default card projects badges into the meta row (`.et-match-card-badges`, end-aligned before live/kick-off), and their labels join `matchName` as `badges` (document order). B220b uncommitted-rebase mark as built (2026-11-14): when the post-commit hook cannot commit its rebase (or leaves out a file dirty before it), it records the sketch folder and commit in the gitignored `<product>/rebase-uncommitted.json` and drops the entry once it commits that sketch whole. The sketch listing answers `rebaseUncommitted: { commit }` for a recorded sketch while its files are dirty in git (`rebaseUncommittedOf`), and the Studio tree row warns `Rebase nach <sha> nicht committet` with the badge `rebase not committed`. Verified live in a git-initialised scratch copy with a failing pre-commit: zoom-chip edit -> 5 sketches rebased, commit refused, all 5 rows warn with that tooltip; committing the sketch files clears it. Specs: hook spec, `rebase-uncommitted.spec.ts`, system-tree spec.

As built (update-dialog height, 2026-11-16): no app change; the STATUS row ("Design 400 px hoch, App 96 px: Ursache offen") was stale. Cause (measured): the 400 px is the design's context frame, not the dialog. `shared/window.ts` `studioWindow` draws the dialog inside a 1440×400 window (`h-100 w-360`) with the title bar; the harness mounts the bare `UpdateDialogComponent`, 320×96. Measured on the design shot of `open`: frame 1440×400, dialog pane 322×98 (320×96 content plus the 1 px pane border). Live, in the built app (`withStudio`, Linux chrome, `update_ready` answered): pane 322×98, content 320×96, in `open` and `long-version`; the pane interior inset by 6 px is pixel-identical to the design in both states (0 of 26660 px differ). Proof path: `design compare` cannot judge this part. It fails all 4 judged states with "the design draws 1 overlay pane, the app opened 0", because the opener (the title bar's Update button) is outside the part and the harness mounts the dialog without a pane; the 6 interaction states are skipped as unchanged SDK controls. The live shot is the proof. Finding (Cause, measured): the pane sits 2 px left and 2 px lower in the design (x 1018, y 40) than in the app (x 1020, y 38). The design places the mock by hand (`absolute top-10 right-25` in `update-dialog.ts`); the SDK anchored-dialog strategy puts it at offset 10 below the trigger (trigger bottom 28), end-aligned with the trigger's right edge (1342). Not changed: moving the pane would mean hand-positioning the SDK overlay in the app; the fix belongs in the design mock (anchor it at the strategy geometry), a design edit that makes merged/ready stale. Verified: `design check --product studio --part components/update-dialog` 0 findings; compare run (4 FAILED as above, action check ok); live shots of `open` and `long-version`. Not verified: interaction states live, compare at tolerance 0 (it cannot run here), macOS/Windows chrome.

584\. Builder (2026-11-07, 994dd8bea): `addedBaselineNamesOf` flagged every entry that some older version of
`rule-baseline.json` did not hold, so only the first commit of the file could baseline anything and a second new rule
could never baseline its old hits (against ADR 0201). No spec covered a second rule. Fixed in 994dd8bea: an entry
counts as added only if an older version already held the same rule without it, with a spec for a second new rule.
Lesson: a decision that names a ratchet ("may only shrink") gets a spec for its second use, not only its first. Built in 994dd8bea.

647\. Builder (2026-11-09, item 0): the Large case "a sketch scroll never empties a cell" fails under 8-worker load in
about 3 of 10 full runs, and blocked the push-suite on 99dda96f7 (e2e 132/133). Alone it passes 4 of 4. A cell loses
its iframe for 30-300 ms after a scroll under CPU load, so this is probably a Studio defect under load, not a test
defect (not proven). Why no tool caught it: the repeat gate runs the suite three times on one load level, so a fault
that needs CPU pressure passes until the load is high by chance. Tool fix (part of item 0, decided by the doc agent
under the anti-stall rule because it blocks the push): fix the empty cell at its cause in Studio; then the e2e runner
gets a load mode (CPU pressure on purpose) that the repeat gate runs, so a load fault fails every time and not one
push in three.

827\. Linux builder (2026-11-11, push:suite at c373dcfd0): "Not formatted in c373dcfd0: package.json"; the 820 subagent
added a script out of key order and reported prettier clean without running it on `package.json`. Cause (read,
`.husky/pre-commit:43`): pre-commit runs prettier only on staged Markdown blobs, so an unformatted `.json` or `.ts` file is
caught one round later by pre-push or push:suite. Tool fix (doc agent, tool internal): pre-commit runs `prettier --check`
on every staged Prettier-supported blob. Bite: a staged unformatted `package.json` fails the commit.

change. Target: a run under 1 s on studio. If that fails, sending the sketch problems later (830 option b) changes what
the human sees and goes to the human as a question.
835 as built (Linux builder, 2026-11-11, this commit: perf(cli) "Parse and scan each source once per text"): profile
first, on a scratch checkout of studio (91 parts, 2 ready sketches, 6 variants, 3 with `shared/`): one run is 10 full
rule runs (product 1, variants 6, merged layout 3) of 35 rules, about 600 ms each; cold 7.0-7.6 s, after a part edit
5.7-6.9 s. Cause (profiled): every rule run re-walks the syntax tree and re-scans the text of every source (definitionOf
1.0-1.5 s, Tailwind class texts 1.4-2.4 s, part rewrites 0.6-1.0 s with a fresh parse each call, command text 0.6-1.0 s,
reachable files 0.5-0.8 s, orphan endpoints 0.4-0.7 s over the 600 KB app source); plus, cold only, the Tailwind
class-facts subprocess 1.35-1.45 s. Why a variant reads all 91 sources: the rules are product-wide (imports, reachable
files, orphan endpoints, shared files) and the variant answer is the difference of two whole-product runs, so narrowing
the read set stays unsound. Built: `perSource` in `ts-source.ts`, a 512-text memo of a pure function of a source text,
on `sourceFileOf`, the node list, `textsOf`, `importsOf`, `calledNamesOf`, `definitionOf`, the Tailwind class texts, part
rewrites, command text, top-level awaits, stylesheet imports, inline UI, glued interpolations, phase unions and
hard-coded colours; the orphan-endpoint verdict is held per app while its sources read the same. Files are still read
each run, so the tracked inputs do not change. Measured (script over `readOpenPoints`, scratch, idle): after a part edit
5.7-6.9 s to 650 ms; cold 7.0-7.6 s to 2.6 s; repeat 35 ms. Not met: cold stays at 2.6 s, of it the Tailwind subprocess
1.4 s and the first parse 0.5 s (suspect: a disk cache of the class facts keyed by their read prints would fix it).
Output byte-equal to HEAD for studio, sdk and studio-lab. Bite: `open-points-reparse.spec.ts` records each syntax-tree
walk after a part edit; red on HEAD source (3 unchanged sources walked again), green after; spec:stress 4/4. Not
verified: a live `/__design/open-points` ask on a server, Studio e2e.

899\. Linux builder (2026-11-11 night, B249 e2e 4c under `--hold-listings 14000`): the merged part's frame stayed empty.
Cause (probe + spec bite `canvas-frame-grid.component.spec.ts`): the `settledCells` linkedSignal of a state grid took an
inline source that read `grid()`; an equal re-read of the frames (held listing) reset the loaded count 7 -> 0, and loaded
imgs never fire `load` again, so the grid never revealed. Pre-existing, not from 487e24844. Built 57bac0dc0: the source is
a computed `shotsKey`. Suspect "aborted shot requests" refuted. Bite 883: with `leaveGone` reverted, 4c times out at the
open-part wait. Lesson: no spec set an equal grid input again while pictures load, and nothing flags a linkedSignal source
written as an inline function over an input (one more site: `loadedShot` in `canvas-frame.component.ts`, harmless). Tool
fix: a lint rule that asks for a computed source there. Open for the human (morning round): the rule would go into the
published `@ethlete/eslint-plugin`, so it changes lint for every consumer. Queue: tool backlog until decided.

7f built (Linux, 6700dfd3d components + core, 00abccaea cli): a loading button keeps its normal colours; the
`aria-disabled` look skips `[data-loading='true']`. Bite: new e2e `button / loading look` failed 4/4 without the fix,
passed 4/4 with it. A disabled `<a>` that loads now looks normal (clicks stay blocked); decided by the doc agent: accept,

## As built: B339 Sketches e2e rule (2026-11-04)

Commit: the one that holds this section (`test(repo): Allow kept unchanged marks before the full sketch compare`).

- The case "no state is marked before the compare answers" now runs on the Chip page only. Its fixture is the
  scratch checkout's `components/zoom-chip` sketch whose variant a sets `reset` to 110 %, so 4 states differ and 12 are
  unchanged. No real sketch is needed; the old `pages/system` sketch dependency is gone from this case.
- It first asks the design server for a full listing (the kept comparison), reloads with the full listing held and the
  quick listing let through, and passes when every mark shown before the full listing answers equals what that earlier
  full listing says for the same state. A mark that listing does not produce is a new mark and fails. After the full
  listing it waits for that answer itself (the old wait on "pending" marks returned too early and left `listed` unset,
  which was the "no listed sketch" message) and then checks every mark against the full listing as before.
- Bites: a temporary route patch dropped `fit` from the quick listing's `unchanged`; the case failed with
  `a/fit marked true before the compare`. The patch is reverted and not committed.
- Not verified: the CI job for `studio:e2e` (B339 stays open for it); the `pages/system` and `shell-main` pages no
  longer run this case, as their sketches are all-unchanged copies and show no variant marks.

## As built: B343 (findings 400, 404)

- Stale counts embedded parts: `sketch/stale-base.ts` finds every product part a variant's held parts reach through
  imports; a change there makes the sketch stale. `design check`, `sketch check` (new: prints `SKETCH-BASE-STALE`
  and fails) and the inbox name that part, and the merge refusal (Studio "… hat sich seit dem Sketch geändert") names
  it too, not the sketch's own target.
- Every merge (`mergeSketch`, the one path of CLI merge, Studio merge button, merge step and auto-merge) calls
  `rebaseAfterMerge`: each undiscarded sketch whose stale parts the merge changed is ported and rebased, re-checked
  when files were ported, and keeps its status (`REBASED <product> <sketch> after the merge of <part>`). On a
  conflict or a failing re-check it gets `portAfterMerge` in `sketch.json` (merged parts, parts, reasons) and the
  merge prints `AGENT PORTS …`; the inbox still lists it as a rebase item. `sketch rebase` clears the mark.
- `sketch rebase`: a part `shared/` file is compared with the copy the sketch lifted into its `shared/` folder, and
  relative shared imports are compared as `@shared/` (cause of finding 404: the variant held the change, but in the
  lifted copy, so the rebase saw a deleted file).
- Specs (each failed before the code): `after-merge.spec.ts` (embedded merge rebases and keeps ready; conflict marks
  and prints), `rebase-port.spec.ts` (lifted shared file identical is clean; product change ports into the lifted
  copy), `sketch-command.spec.ts` (embedded change: `sketch check` prints SKETCH-BASE-STALE naming elements/hero).
  "Identical content in the part's own file" passed before already (the old code compared bytes).
- Studio draws the "Agent portiert nach Merge von <part>" line from the listing's `portAfterMerge` (B502).

## As built: B377 (ADR 0192)

- `yarn studio:e2e` builds Studio once, then runs the cases on workers: each a forked process with its own scratch checkout, design server (free port via `DE_PORT`) and Chromium. Workers pull cases from one queue, slowest first by the timings of the last run (`node_modules/.cache/studio-e2e/canvas-timings.json`). Every case already reloads the page and clears localStorage, and the only shared state is the checkout, so any case can run on any worker.
- Default: `min(8, cores / 4)` workers (8 here); `--workers <n>` or `STUDIO_E2E_WORKERS` overrule it. `--case <name>` still works. The workers run with `ETHLETE_DESIGN_SLOW_CHECKS=off`.
- The run ends with the time per page group and per case, slowest first.
- `tools/scripts/verify-studio-headless.mjs` exports `ensureCli` and `buildStudio`.
- Wall time: 12 min 10 s serial (B367b) -> 2 min 27 s (8 workers, slow checks on, 113/114: System "a frame renders real content" saw empty frames), 1 min 56 s (12 workers, load peak 46, 113/114: Sketches "ctrl-wheel keeps the world point" drifted 86 px), 2 min 9 s (8 workers, final, load peak 38, 114/114).
- Flaky cases: Sketches "pan beyond every edge" and Large "a variant equal to Aktuell" passed in all 3 parallel runs.
- cli vitest: no config change. Default (31 forks) 97 s, `--maxWorkers=16` 91 s; CPU about 50 % idle in both. The run is bound by `check-system.spec.ts` alone (89-95 s); splitting that file is the lever.
- Not verified: a serial run of the new runner (only the B367b number as "before"), more than one run per worker count.

## As built: B249 slice 5a, edit sketch old/new (D1, D2) (2026-11-11, Linux)

- D1 cause, proven by the `edit-sketch.spec.ts` case "takes old from the part at HEAD when no commit holds its merged
  hash" (failed before: `expected undefined to deeply equal [ 'new', 'old' ]`, EDIT-OLD-NOT-FOUND): `oldDesignOf` only
  took a commit whose rebuilt part hash equals the `merged.json` hash, and a drifted hash is in no commit. Fix:
  `old` is the part folder at HEAD. Why: ADR 0256 records every committed state of a merged part as merged, so HEAD
  holds the last merged design; reading it needs no hash, so drift cannot lose it, and there is no history walk. A part
  HEAD holds no file of still gets the new-only sketch and EDIT-OLD-NOT-FOUND. Specs that expected old from an older
  commit for a committed edit now expect HEAD (ADR 0256).
- D2 cause, proven by the `unchanged-states.spec.ts` case "names no state of the edit sketch variant new when the sketch
  has no old" (failed before: `expected [ 'default' ] to deeply equal []`): `new` of an edit sketch is the product
  itself, so every state compared unchanged and Studio folded all. Fix: `unchangedStatesOf` /
  `keptUnchangedStatesOf` answer no unchanged state for an edit sketch without `old`; with `old` the fold already
  needs `old` to draw the same as `new`. No app change.
- Verified: `vitest related` on the changed files (132 files, 1356 tests), `nx run cli:typecheck`, eslint, prettier.
  Live on a scratch checkout (own git, HEAD `merged.json` with zoom-chip at the drifted `eac0eac1e633a857`, cli
  built there, server on :4733): design "Fit" -> "Fit all" opened `components/zoom-chip@edit` with `new` and `old`
  in 21 s; `/__design/sketches` answers `unchanged: []` for `old`, so no state folds; `/__design/shot` of state
  `fit` shows "Fit" (old) and "Fit all" (new).
- Not verified: the Studio app sketch view (no Studio build; the fold reads only the `unchanged` lists), the pick of
  `new` (check 4c), D3 (Verwerfen on `@edit`).

## As built: B249 slice 5c-1, serve writes no tracked file (D6), no discard on `@edit` (S6b) (2026-11-11, Linux)

- D6 cause, proven by bites: the serve slow runner called `settleCommittedEdits` and `autoAcceptOf`, and both call
  `recordMerged`; the settle path also deleted an edit sketch even when git tracks it. Suspect for the live run: the
  tree-row write was the HELD path (uncommitted edit that draws as before), the zoom-chip write the settle path (HEAD
  holds the part after the revert; matches "both edit sketches were removed").
- Fix: `writesTracked: false` on `settleCommittedEdits` and `autoAcceptOf`, set by the slow runner. In that mode a
  held or settled edit is not recorded (stays "changed outside a sketch" for `design check`, which still records it),
  an edit sketch is deleted only when git tracks no file in it and no comment is on it, a held edit writes no
  `pictures.json` record (the drawing stays in the untracked part-picture cache), and a tracked edit sketch is not
  refreshed. The slow runner remembers each resolved edit hash in memory, so it does not redraw it on every poll.
- S6b: `editDiscardRefusalOf` (`edit-sketch.ts`); `POST /__design/sketch-discard` answers 422 reason
  `edit-discard-refused`, `sketch discard` exits 1; both with `EDIT-DISCARD-REFUSED: <part>@edit ... pick old to undo
the edit or new to keep it`. The internal discard of `design check` is unchanged.
- Bites (each failed on the old code): slow-run "writes no tracked file for a committed direct edit and its committed
  edit sketch" (temp git repo, `git status --untracked-files=no` clean) and the reworded "deletes an untracked edit

  file when told so"; `studio-sketch-discard.spec.ts` "refuses the old/new sketch of a direct edit"; sketch-command
  "refuses to discard the old/new sketch of a direct edit".

## As built: B249 slice 5c-1b, serve keeps the same-drawing verdict in memory (2026-11-11, Linux)

- Cause, proven by the bite: with `writesTracked: false` a held edit is not recorded, and every open-points reader used
  `changedOutsideSketchOf`, which compares only with `merged.json`; so serve showed a held edit as `direct-edit`.
- Fix: `sketch/held-edits.ts` keeps, per product, each part the slow runner held with its part hash (`autoAcceptOf`
  hands them out through the new `held` option). `openDirectEditPartsOf` drops a part whose hash still equals the held
  one; `directEditsOf` (open points, build-ready, `ready.json`), `directEdit` of the part answer and the system listing
  use it. The server sends its held edits with every open-points worker request, and the open-points cache keys on
  them. `changedOutsideSketchOf` is unchanged, so `design check` and the recording paths still see the edit.
- Bites: slow-run "shows no open point for a direct edit that draws as before while it runs, and writes no tracked
  file" failed before (`directEdit` true, `direct-edit` point); it also failed with the worker sync removed. Guard:
