505\. Tom's merge of `components/title-bar@notice-hint` (pick b) was refused a third time (findings 434, 468): "studio has
uncommitted edits outside components/title-bar@notice-hint ... ready.json, rule-baseline.json". `rule-baseline.json`
was cb's staged B401; `ready.json` held a `components/canvas-viewport` ready mark at 09:44:55Z that no running session
wrote (likely c0's `sketch ready` measurements on `pages/system` before its restart). The doc agent saved both to its
scratchpad, reset them, Tom merged (332e49626), and `rule-baseline.json` went back byte-identical. Why no tool caught
it: the merge checks the whole tree, so any foreign uncommitted file blocks it, and the process rule of finding 434 did
not hold with three builders; the `by` field decided in finding 468 was never built because the finding got no STATUS
row. Tool fix: the merge checks in a clean copy of HEAD plus the sketch (ADR 0206, B406); every ready-mark and pick

507\. `verify pages/start` reported NO RECORD: five merged studio parts (components/disclosure,
components/update-dialog, elements/shell-main, pages/inventory, pages/start) had a design hash that no longer matched
`merged.json`. Source-only commits changed them and never re-ran the picture check: the withAction refactors
d961cb00d, b826f7096, 4bbd88e03, 32aaf6552, 5bec01b89, and the chore fea9ac862, which did change shell-main's look (it
embeds the title bar, so pages/start moves with it). Why no tool caught it: pre-push runs only `design check --rules`,
and no rule compares a merged part's hash with `merged.json`. Fix (B412, ADR 0036/0037: a check-system rule, not a
hook gate): a rule reports DIRECT-EDIT-PENDING on every merged part whose hash moved without a `merged.json` record;
it shows as a problem on the part (not build-ready) and fails `--rules` in pre-push and CI. The five parts are closed
by `design check --product studio --part <each>`: auto-accept for the four with no visible change, an old/new edit
sketch for shell-main (and start through the embed) that waits for Tom's pick (ADR 0135).
Follow-up: `design check --part` closed none of the five. A committed direct edit was a dead end: auto-accept had no
pictures at the merged hash and opened an edit sketch with `old` = HEAD, which already holds the edit, so old == new
and `edit-sketch.ts` refused ("HEAD holds the edit ... no old design to show"). Why no tool caught it: the edit-sketch
specs covered only uncommitted direct edits. Fix (B412): `old` = the part's files at the newest commit whose part hash
equals `merged.json[part]`, not HEAD; with no such commit the part shows a problem with a hint, never a silent dead
end. Picking `old` writes that version back (ADR 0135).
As built (507, builder c0, 2026-11-06): `edit-sketch.ts` walks `git log` over the part folder and the product's
`shared/` and `assets/` folders, rebuilds those folders of each commit in a temp dir and hashes the part there with
`partHashOf`; the newest commit with the merged hash gives `old`, for a new edit sketch and for `refreshEditOld`. No
such commit: rule EDIT-OLD-NOT-FOUND on the part, with the `et design accept` command as the hint. A pick of `old`
merges those files back. Verified: specs with a temp git repo (committed refactor holds, committed edit gets the old
files, pick old writes them back, no matching commit gives the problem); they fail on the old HEAD code. Not verified:
`design check` on the five studio parts, and the speed of the walk on the real history.
As built (part 1, builder, 2026-11-06, 3e10f1ddf + type fix 6d26ac045): `old` comes from the newest commit whose part
hash equals `merged.json[part]`; with none, the rule EDIT-OLD-NOT-FOUND shows on the part with the hint `et design
accept <part> --product <p> --by ... --note ...`; picking `old` writes those files back. Real run: components/disclosure
HELD (80f953c0c); components/update-dialog (a383f2bdb drew the button states after the merge), pages/inventory and
elements/shell-main (title bar embed fea9ac862) open `@edit` sketches; pages/start has EDIT-OLD-NOT-FOUND (no commit
holds merged hash 5074133a3524678e) and waits for Tom's accept as it is. Open: the DIRECT-EDIT-PENDING rule lands
after Tom's picks, else it blocks every push; disclosure's pictures.json entry moved from key `go` to `record` (cause
asked; answered: `go` is a legacy kind still read, the rewrite kept hash and pictures, no data loss).

508\. 3e10f1ddf did not compile: a subagent committed CLI code without running tsc, and `git commit` runs no

tool caught it: no local gate runs a typecheck before a commit lands on `next`. Fix now: every builder brief to a
subagent names a tsc step (or `yarn commit`). No pre-push typecheck: Tom already moved typecheck to CI only (ADR 0038).

line names the near miss (`design draws combobox "…" in components/select - accessible names differ`); (c) later
slice B413: an ACCESSIBLE-NAME drift rule.
As built (b) (c0, 2026-11-06): `ownScopeOf` leaves an app element to the embedded part when its role has one leftover
element on each side (shared `renamedPairsOf` with `pairElementsOf`); a failure without a partner names the same-role

511\. `design check --slow --part X` did not write the check record; only a fast `check --part X` afterwards did

asserts that each check mode writes the record. Fix: `--slow` writes the same record as the fast check (it runs a

Not verified: a whole-product `--slow` run live (it now also runs the full check).

516\. Tom's "q1ok" for pages/sketches reached the builder only as a relayed message, and the builder's permission
check refused `accept --by tom`: an agent may not record Tom's consent from a relay. The doc agent had promised the
accept in Tom's name. Why no tool caught it: the Tom-only accept exists only as a CLI flag an agent types; nothing
lets Tom grant it with one action of his own. Fix: Studio lists the open `@edit` picks in one place with one
"Übernehmen" button per item, so Tom clicks instead of an agent typing `--by tom` (layout as a sketch for Tom). Until
then Tom runs the accept himself with `!` in a session. The doc agent no longer offers "ok in chat" for a Tom-only
accept.

517\. The doc agent put a process question to Tom (do plan decisions count for an agent accept, ADR 0210) that
followed from his own ADR 0209. Tom: "q2ok aber das solltest du entscheiden. du schreibst schon wieder klingonisch mit
mir". Two defects: (1) a question that extends an existing decision in its own spirit is the doc agent's to decide and
report, not to ask; (2) the German text to Tom was full of internal ids (ADR numbers, Impl Q, `@edit`, `--by tom`,
part paths). Why no tool caught it: the doc-agent skill limits ids for sessions only (finding 506), not for ADRs,
flags and plan refs, and it says to put tool and process decisions to Tom without a test for "follows from an
existing decision". Fix (doc-agent skill, builder edits it): text to Tom says what a thing is in plain words (an ADR
number at most in brackets after the plain statement, no flags, no plan refs); a question that applies an existing
decision to a new case is decided by the doc agent and reported in one line.

800\. Linux builder (2026-11-11, night, push of 0884cf03c): pre-push refused the push with "push slot held by
linux-builder for 0884cf03c25d ... Wait for its push or expiry", and the holder was the builder itself. Cause (measured):
`ETHLETE_BUILDER` was set only in the push:suite shell, so pre-push took the hostname as the name and saw a foreign
holder; the message told the builder to wait 60 min for its own slot. Why no tool caught it: 780 keys the slot on a name
that two shells of one builder can set differently, and its specs used one environment. Lesson: identify the holder by
what it proved (the sha and its suite verdict), not by a name the caller may not set. Decided by the doc agent (tool
internal, the builder's proposal): pre-push accepts the slot when the slot sha equals the pushed sha and a local
push-suite ok verdict exists for that sha; otherwise the refusal names the holder and says "set ETHLETE_BUILDER=<holder>
if this is you". Bite: a push with no `ETHLETE_BUILDER` after a suite ok for the same sha passes; a different sha is
refused with the hint. Night backlog, Linux, after 799; the Mac must pull it before its next push.

800 as built: `push-slot.mjs check "$local_sha"` (the hook passes the pushed sha as an argument, so the loop's stdin stays
untouched and `git push origin <sha>:next` works). `checkSlot` passes for the holder name, or when the slot sha equals
the pushed sha and `.git/push-suite/<sha>` (the file push-suite writes) starts with `ok `; the refusal ends with "Set
ETHLETE_BUILDER=<holder> if this is you." Bite: the new "slot sha with ok verdict, other name" spec fails with the sha
rule removed, passes with it; the different-sha and no-verdict specs also pass. The spec's git helper strips `GIT_*`.
Verified: `node --test tools/scripts/push-slot.spec.mjs` (9 pass), eslint clean. Not verified: a real pre-push run
against origin; the Mac must pull before its next push.

811\. Linux builder (2026-11-11, from the Mac): `design check --product studio` on a clean HEAD 87c279030 rewrote the committed `.ethlete/design/studio/ready.json` (+20/-136): "RECORD DROPPED" for foundations/colors, foundations/spacing and pages/inventory, each with an OFF-CENTRE problem "found by design check". OFF-CENTRE has a rule baseline (d8cf6cd80, ADR 0201): a baselined old hit must not drop a ready record. Suspect until reproduced: either the baseline misses these 3 parts, or the ready auto-accept path reads the render result without the baseline.
811 not reproduced on Linux (Linux builder, 2026-11-11), stays Suspect: in a HEAD export (0afe96985) with its own cli build and an empty `node_modules/.cache`, `design check --product studio --part` for foundations/colors, foundations/spacing and pages/inventory each printed "clean", 0 findings, and kept all 3 records; the full `design check --product studio` had no OFF-CENTRE hit in studio, no RECORD DROPPED, and only added or refreshed records (foundations/logo, foundations/type, pages/inventory). The code path matches ADR 0201: `renderSystem` tallies only the OFF-CENTRE issues the rule baseline does not list, and `withTalliedProblems` turns only those into "found by design check" blockers. So on the Mac those 3 parts most likely hit OFF-CENTRE without a baseline entry: the check measures text against font metrics, and the baseline was recorded on Linux. Next step: run the Mac check with `--part foundations/colors` and keep the OFF-CENTRE line it prints (state, size, element path), so the hit is either fixed or baselined.

811 on the Mac (Mac builder subagent, 2026-11-11, measured in a worktree with a patched copy of the rule). Cause (measured): the flagged text is set in `10px ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace` (`--font-code` in `.ethlete/design/studio/foundations/type/type.css`); the design frame loads no web font (`document.fonts.size` 0, status `loaded`), so the Mac draws SF Mono and Linux the generic `monospace`. SF Mono at 10px: ascent 9, descent 2, cap 7.29, an 11px line box. In the 22px content box of `co-ratio` and `sp-height` the 11px slack splits 5/6, so above 7.71 and below 9.0 (1.29 > the 1px tolerance); in the 16px `pages/inventory` box the slack splits 0/1 (3.71 / 5.0). The same font makes most `pages/sketches` `sk-gutter` gaps 0.65-0.95px, so their baseline entries no longer hit on the Mac. Not the cause: font load timing (no web fonts). Not measured: the Linux fallback numbers. Recommendation: self-host one monospace font and the UI font in the design styles, so both OSes measure the same font; a per-OS baseline entry (ADR 0201) keeps two truths and still drops records on the other OS; a tool fix in the rule removes only the 0.29px font share, not the 1px layout split. Side result: the main checkout's `dist/libs/cli` was stale against HEAD and the CLI gate refused it.

The canvas text e2e case now checks each text's glyph box against its clipping boxes top and bottom; bite: fails on Inbox and System with the old classes, passes with the fix. As built (B462 stale picture): the e2e case „a sketch cell edited on disk while scrolled away shows its new picture on return“ read the first `img` of the cell, which is the old picture the sketch view keeps on top until the new one loads; under load the new shot drew in over 10 s (CI 44095404324). The census now also reports `wantedPictureSrc` (`img[data-shot-picture]`), and the case waits on it. Measured: the `parts` event names elements/shell-main 26-70 ms after the edit. Bite: shot responses delayed 12 s after the edit, old read 0/2, new read 2/2.

As built (B559, ADR 0331): PAGE-STATE-INNER draws each state of an own page outside a browser and splits the markup by owner: the page's own markup (including markup it passes into a part, `data-et-slot`) and each embedded part instance (`data-et-part`, the marked named exports included). A state fails when its page markup equals that of the default state, or of a state whose props it all repeats, and the differences sit in one part instance; the message names the innermost part holding them all. Two changed sibling parts, or any change to the page's own markup, pass. It is a draw rule in the `--slow` set (ADR 0201). Findings: studio pages/system `send-busy` (only components/comment-draft, which already has `busy`) dropped; pages/sketches `paused-reason` changed the page's own reason span, so the rule did not see it: the reason moved into components/hold-trigger (`reason` prop, its `open` state shows it), the page passes it and drops the state, and the capability `sketch-paused-reason` now sits on hold-trigger `emit:openChange`. sdk and studio-lab: no hits.

### B560 as built (ADR 0332)

`nestingHostOf` drops the same-layer limit; `treeOf` works hosts out once over every placed part, so a part with one
user nests under it in any group, with `TreeEntry.layer` (its layer label) when the host's layer differs. A host outside
the tree or in `unused` leaves the part in its layer; `unused` sections nest within their layer only; base parts and
parts with 2+ users never nest. tree-row draws the tag (`mark-layer`, `selected-layer`), part-tree shows it
(`cross-layer`: hold-trigger under pages/sketches); app tree-row/part-tree mirror it. Verified: vitest related 368 pass,
app tsc, check --part tree-row/part-tree 0 findings. Not verified: live Studio shot; `design task --verify` runs after
the commit (DIRECT EDIT open point blocks the check record before it).

hold-trigger grid (closed/open x rest/hover/active/focus-visible). `shared/diff-grid.ts` derives the marked region
of each cell from its difference to closed rest (interaction: the trigger, open: the reason, both: the whole part);

As built (pages/sketches ready): not ready. `design ready` marked it (254979f7b, which also took 5 marks a design serve
had written; restored 4677112b7; merged hash adeb6ffd0), but `design check --part pages/sketches` still finds
CANVAS-UNDER-PANEL and 2x ARROW-ANCHOR in `change-crop` and `change-crop-whole`, so the mark was dropped b4da6b459.
Cause (proven in a scratch probe): the mock screen draws 12 zoom chips, and both the frame aim
(`libs/cli/design/arrow-anchor.ts` `anchorOf`) and the check (`system/arrow-anchor.ts`) resolve
`data-et-arrow-anchor` with `root.querySelector`, so the Fit tooltip is measured against the first chip's fit button.
Resolving from the nearest ancestor that holds a match cleared both ARROW-ANCHOR hits. CANVAS-UNDER-PANEL: the aim's
device-pixel rounding gives the tooltip wrapper `translate: 0.25px -0.16px`; it is wider than its 42px span, and the
span inherits `cursor: grab` from the canvas, so `holdsPannedWorld` counts the tooltip above the button as a pan
world. Proposed: count a moved child as a world only when it overlaps the viewport box. Both fixes are libs/cli check
changes, which the builder slice may not make (refused); open for the cli owner.
Suspect, not probed: `design ready` passed on the same tree that `check --part` fails, so the ready gate may read a
cached or narrower render result. Verified: probe check in a scratch copy with the anchor scoping (ARROW-ANCHOR 0) and
a debug line naming the panned child. Not verified: the overlap fix, a cli spec, a live Studio shot.

As built (B576 slice 1, ADR 0335): cause (by probe) - `keepHeldStampsInFiles` composed a check run's ready.json onto
`diskStampTextOf`, which is the design server's stamp cache (`.ethlete/cache/<product>/stamps/ready.json`) while its
base matches the tracked file, so every serve mark in that cache landed in the tracked file. A `check --part
elements/part-tree` whose own record changed wrote 14 foreign marks (13 `cmd: serve`, plus studio-menu). The writer now
composes onto the tracked text and takes the asked keys (`check --part` / `parts`, `'all'` for a whole-product check);
an entry outside them is never written. `design ready` and the dropped-record commit commit HEAD's ready.json plus the
own entry only (`commitOwnEntry` in part-ready.ts); the working file keeps every other entry. A check still writes the
asked part's mark (ADR 0335 asks for "only", not "none"). Verified: stamp-files.spec (asked keys, no cache entry) and
part-ready.spec (ready commits only its own mark), each red with its fix reverted. Live, from the same clean ready.json
and stamp cache: the published cli (c510481c6) dropped part-tree and wrote 14 foreign marks; `--working-tree` dropped
part-tree only. Not verified: a live `design ready` commit (no ready-clean part to spend on it).

As built (B576 slice 2, ADR 0335): probe first, on the live studio product (37 holding marks). (1) Another part's

or harness.shared; it covers the files of the part's import graph (`designHashOf`), each whole. Suspect not reproduced.
(2) An export nobody imports appended to `title-bar/shared/chrome.ts`: 9 marks stale (whole-file grain); export-level

checks and re-decide every own part (`recordedPartsOf`). The `(product)` inputs now key on each part's recorded
`actions`, which is what ACTION-LOST reads. The stale page marks seen on 17.11. are real dependency drops (studio-menu,

As built (B576 slice 3, ADR 0335): cause (by spec bite) - `design ready` and `design check --part` drew the same

As built (B577 slice 1, ADR 0336): cause (by spec bite) - `settleCommittedEdits` (accepted-pictures.ts) took only
undecided `@edit` sketches, so a picked one whose part HEAD holds (live: `elements/studio-menu@edit`, picked `new`,
committed) was named STALE EDIT SKETCH and left for a discard the classifier refuses, while status also printed
SKETCH-BASE-STALE with a rebase that `@edit` has no use for. Now the settle takes every ready `@edit` sketch, undecided
or picked, without hold or rejection (`isOpenOrPickedEditSketch`, edit-sketch.ts): check, ready and the design server
delete it once HEAD holds its part. `staleSketchBasesOf` skips a stale edit sketch, and status names it once as SKETCH
LEFTOVER with the check that clears it. Verified: accepted-pictures.spec (picked new + committed, picked old +
restored, a `writesTracked: false` run) and status-uncommitted.spec, red with the fix reverted. Live: status
printed one line for studio-menu@edit, and `design check --product studio --part elements/studio-menu` deleted it
(STALE EDIT SKETCH ... discarded). Not verified: a picked `old` whose HEAD holds the `new` edit also closes silently.

As built (B577 slice 2, ADR 0336): cause (by spec bite) - `portBaseChanges` (rebase-port.ts) ported every variant
from the baseline to the working part, `old` of an `@edit` too; its baseline is the working tree at open, so a later
working-tree change was taken or 3-way merged into `old` (the part at HEAD), and a change on the edited line was an
`old` conflict that only `--ported old` passed. Now the port skips `old` of an `@edit` sketch: it stays the part at
HEAD, `new` takes the change. Verified: edit-sketch.spec (a change in another file leaves `old` at HEAD and the pick
of old works; a change on the edited line rebases without a conflict), both red with the skip removed. Not verified:
a live rebase on an `@edit` (no live sketch touched); `old` does not follow a HEAD that moved since open - the

As built (B577 slice 3, ADR 0336): cause (by spec bite) - slice 1 settled a picked `@edit` once HEAD held its part,

and status-uncommitted.spec (picked old: the merge line), red with the fix reverted; the slice 1 status spec decided a
stale sketch object, so its pick was refused and it ran undecided - fixed. Not verified: a live picked `old` with `new`

## As built (B236)

Cause (finding 289): a part-scoped check drew and checked only the asked part, so `check --part
elements/canvas-frames` passed while pages/system broke. Fix (check-system.ts `checkEmbedders`): after `check --part X`
(single part, not `--base`), each part that embeds X is checked on the same warm draw, browser and typecheck: render
rules, its static rules and the draw-rule tail, without auto-accept, open points, slow settle or ready marks, and
without the product-level TYPE-ERROR and warnings X's own run already printed. A failing embedder prints its `PART`
line; the run ends with `EMBEDDERS PASS X: n parts` or `EMBEDDERS FAIL X: k of n - ...; X is not ready until they
pass`, exits 1, and drops X's ready mark. Choices: embedders are transitive by the import graph (`embeddedPartsOf`, the
graph ready marks key on, ADR 0340), base parts skipped. Embedders are not asked parts (ADR 0335): their marks are
neither written nor dropped; only X's mark is dropped. X's own output is unchanged; clean embedders add a progress line
each and the PASS line after `check complete`. Verified: check-embedders.spec (transitive embedders; a COVERED
embedder fails X and drops its mark, an unrelated part checks no embedders, passing embedders keep X's exit), red with
the call or the drop reverted. Live: `check --part elements/canvas-frames` checked pages/inbox (UNRECORDED, fails) and
pages/system (2 warnings, passes); 19 s before, 24 s after; ready.json changed only the asked part's mark. Not verified:
a product with many embedders (pages each run their own render job in turn, not one batched job).

## As built (B243)

Cause (finding 295): a merge made 20 embedding parts stale and neither named nor checked them, so "no new problem from
the merge" had no baseline. Fix (`sketch/merge-embedders.ts` `embedderCheckAroundMerge`, called by `design sketch
merge` and the plan-run merge step): before the merge, the parts that embed a merged part (the sketch's targets plus
the picked variant's parts; `embeddersOfPart`, transitive, base parts skipped, merged parts themselves left out) are
checked silently with B236's embedder check (`embedderProblemCodesOf` in check-system.ts: render, static and tail
rules, no ready marks, stamps in memory) and their problem codes kept per part. Once the merge landed, it prints
`STALE EMBEDDERS <product>: ...`, checks them again and prints one `NEW PROBLEM <part>: <codes>` per part with a code
it did not show before, or `EMBEDDERS NO NEW PROBLEM: n parts`; a part that did not draw before or after gets
`EMBEDDER NOT CHECKED`. Choices: compared by code set per part, so a code already present (any count) is not new; the
baseline is the checkout before the merge (the drawn embedders do not change in a merge, only what they embed); no ADR
decides refusal, so it only reports and the exit code is unchanged; the lines come before the `merged ...` line, which
stays last; the before check is skipped when the sketch is not ready or the variant is unknown, so the cheap refusals
stay fast; the Studio merge (worker) does not run it. Verified: sketch-command.spec "names the parts that embed the
merged one ..." (merging components/button names elements/hero and pages/home, hero's COVERED before and after is not
reported, a CLIPPED in pages/home after the merge is), red with the after-merge call removed; the other merge specs pass
unchanged. Not verified: a live merge on the real design (cost estimated from B236: two embedder checks, about 2-3 s per embedder each).

This only loosens sketch-side false positives, so no sweep over committed sketches and parts (finding 789). Verified:

variant `same` passes, `worse` fails only on its new cell), red before the fix with the inherited problem on both

elements/canvas-frames marks its three plain buttons with `data-et-control` (`reload` in load-failed, `column` for the

## As built (B260)

Probe confirmed the suspect: `sketchRevisionOf` took the newest revision over every variant key of the target, and the
sketch view gave that one `revision` to every variant row, so a redraw of variant `a` changed the src and picture of
variant `b` and reloaded it. Fix (fix(repo): Reload only the frames of the redrawn sketch variant):
`sketchRevisionOf` takes an optional `variant` and then counts only the keys of that variant plus the target as the
product has it; system-view passes `variantRevisions` (one per `sketch.variants` entry) to sketch-view, and
`sketchRowsOf` uses it per variant row, falling back to the sketch-wide revision. The errored flag stays sketch-wide.
Verified: frame-revisions.spec "keeps the revision of a variant when only another variant of the sketch redraws" (red
before: 1 became 2) and system-tree.spec "renews a variant row only with the revision of that variant". Not verified:
a live redraw in the app; the builder takes the shot.

printed "Port 4491 is already in use" and was still running after 90 s (Vite threw, `index.ts` set exit code 1, but the
open Vite server kept the process alive). `serveDesign` now closes the server when `listen` fails and rethrows; live it

(b) Partly done before: `startDesignServer` already rejected on cli exit (6c33ed118), so with (a) the harness fails

Findings 332 and 336(a). (1) Cause (probed): on 2026-11-03 Studio drew the sketch list from the quick listing
(`?unchanged=no`), which then carried no `targets` (studio-api at 0eb774996), and `sketchRowsOf` gives a variant row
without a target the states of the part now. All three variants declared `failed` (variant files at 0eb774996), and
the view took its columns from the union of every row's states, so neither candidate held: the four base states of
a/b/c drew alike and `failed` had no row. system-tree.spec "draws a variant row in the states of the part now while
the listing carries no targets yet" pins that fallback; "gives each variant row a state only the variants declare" shows
it is gone once targets arrive. Done before: f1307c562 (2026-11-04) lists the targets in the quick listing. 336(a):

Grill decision 2026-11-18. Commit `feat(cli): Record who builds a part in ready.json` (sha in the builder's report).

  declaration or a `const` arrow/function); each `inject(<service>)` or non-framework `inject…()` in its body adds

## As built (sketch round --asks)

Decision 78681ea6a (2026-11-02). Commit `feat(cli): Refuse sketch variants that look alike in the states a round asks`.

- `SketchRound.asks` in `sketch.json`; set by `sketch round <target> <round> --asks <state,state>`, `sketch new --asks`
  and `sketch variant --round … --asks` (MCP `sketch_round`/`sketch_new`/`sketch_variant` take `asks`). Absent, a round
  asks in the states its variants draw that Aktuell lacks; when there are none (no notion of "states a round added"
  exists, so this stands in for it), in the states where one of its variants draws differently from Aktuell.
- `alikePairLinesOf` in `look-alike.ts`, called from `sketchRendersOf`: per round, every pair of live variants of that
  round (pairs across rounds are not compared), in each asked state, counts the pixels that differ by `VISIBLE_STEP`
  at 100 % inside the union of the `boxOf` boxes; under 2 % of the frame area in any asked state refuses, naming the
  state with the smallest share. A pair the exact-equality refusal already names is left out. `sketch ready` (via
  `identicalRenderLines`) and `sketch check` (`sketchRenderLines`) both refuse on it; edit sketches and `sketch
withdraw` do not use it. Exact-equality refusals and the fit-zoom warning stay.
- Variant-note region: not built. The tool draws no variant note on a shot (notes live in `sketch.json` and Studio's
  UI); the note text of 78681ea6a was drawn by the variants themselves, so there is no region to ignore.

Rule run (2026-11-18, `yarn et:design --working-tree sketch check` on each open sketch; decided ones not re-gated:
studio-lab `components/card`, `elements/rating`): studio-lab `components/button` (r1, no `asks`) passes. studio
`pages/system` (r1, ready, no pick) is now refused: in the added state `developer-part-blocked` a and b differ by 0 px,
a and c and b and c by 22 px (0.0 %). It is not exempted; the next `sketch ready` of it refuses until the variants
differ there or the round names other `--asks` states.

Verified: look-alike.spec "sketchRendersOf alike pairs" (under 2 % refused, over 2 % passes, default asks the added
state, `asks` replaces it, identical pairs left to that refusal; the two refusal cases red with the share set to 0),
sketch.spec "keeps the states a round asks its question in"; `vitest related` in libs/cli (192 files), lint, typecheck.
Not verified: a live `sketch ready` refusal (only `sketch check`'s "ready will refuse" lines were run).

Decided (doc agent, technical, refines 78681ea6a, 2026-11-18): the 2 % is measured against the region the round
changes, not the whole frame: the union box of every live variant's diff against Aktuell in that asked state. A
whole-frame base cannot be met by a small-region round on a page-sized part (a footer badge on `pages/system` needs
~37k px). A state with no diff against Aktuell keeps the whole frame as its base.
Decided (doc agent, technical, refines the line above, 2026-11-18): a state Aktuell has no shot of (the variants add
it) takes as its base the union box of the pairwise diffs between the live variants in that state. Only a state where
no variant differs from Aktuell nor from another variant keeps the whole frame.

## As built (B251a)

Commit df852b421 `feat(cli): Require loading, error and empty states on data parts`. The first half
of B251: a part outside `foundations/` that loads data (`takesDataOf` in `part-builder.ts`: a B250 `loads data` reason,
an `@angular/common/http` or `@ethlete/query` import or a `fetch`/`resource`/`rxResource`/`httpResource` call, on its
design file or its `implements` component) gets one `missing-state` open point (`{ control: null, data }`) per
loading, error and empty state it does not draw, so it is not build-ready. A state counts when a hyphen word of its
name says it (loading: the ongoing-work words; error: `error`, `errored`, `failed`, `failure`; empty: `empty`, `none`,
`no`), the vocabulary committed parts already use (`load-failed`, `listing-error`, `table-empty`, `no-results`). The
subject is `data:<state>`, so a sketch that draws one of them adds no point (ADR 0095). Studio lists it as "Daten-Part
ohne Zustand Laden/Fehler/Leer". Pages count; a part whose states cannot be read is skipped.

Not covered: a presentational part that gets a list from a loader outside any part (the sketches page of B314: the
listing loads in `system-view`, the page only takes `rows`). An array input as the signal hit about ten Studio parts
that only take fixed lists (window buttons, log lines, tree rows); open for the grill.

Verified: open-points.spec "required data states (B251a)" (red first: 4 of 5 failed), part-builder.spec,
open-points-reparse.spec (it caught the first cut walking every component per read; the reasons are now per source), Studio
open-points.spec, `vitest related` in libs/cli and apps/ethlete-studio, lint; real-open-points budget unchanged and
`et:design --working-tree check` over every product: studio-lab 0, sdk 0, studio 0 hits (no committed part loads data
itself). Not verified: Studio showing the line live (no part hits it).

## As built (B251b)

Decision: findings-2026-11 "Build-ready decisions" items 6 and 8 (ADR 0048, ADR 0010, ADR 0222). Probe on 7236f85fe:
nothing of it was built - the B502a sketches were opened and drawn by hand, and the three `STATE-UNDESIGNED` hits of
studio were stale baseline entries (their sketches merged on 2026-11-15/16), so `design check` reported 3 "no longer
hits" lines and 0 live hits. The entries are removed; no sketch opens for them.

- `undesigned-branches.ts` `missingStateOf`: the state that takes an undesigned branch - the first design state's props
  with each input the branch's conditions read set (input reads, `!`, `&&`/`||` split by the wanted value, `===` with
  a literal), checked with the branch evaluator, named after the last input set (kebab case, `-built` on a clash).
  `null` otherwise. The DROPPED-PROP runner stores it on the hit as `Problem.missing`.
- `sketch/undesigned-sketch.ts` `openUndesignedSketch`: the ready sketch `<part>@<state>`, one variant `built`: the
  part with `export default definePart` turned into `const drawn` and a default export that adds the state and draws
  it as `<state>.built.ts` (the app picture as a PNG data URL); `sketch.json` takes `undesigned: [<branch>]`.
  The picture form is the closest working one: the design server draws markup, so the developer's build enters as
  an image, not as redrawn markup.
- The hit waits: `slowProblemsOf` drops a `STATE-UNDESIGNED` hit an open sketch of its part lists in `undesigned`
  (`withoutWaitingUndesigned`); a pick ends the wait. A pick of `built` merges the state, so the branch is taken and
  the hit clears; a pick of a redrawn variant without that state brings the hit back until the app matches.
- Serve hook: `slow-run.ts` `startSlowRunner` runs `openUndesignedSketches` after each product's slow checks: per hit
  without an open sketch it shoots the app harness at the missing props (`shootBuiltState`) and opens the sketch; a hit
  without `missing` logs that its sketch is drawn by hand.

  missing export/module), lint, `vitest related`.

## As built (B251 built placeholder)

Decision (grill, applies B251, ADR 0048 and ADR 0011): the pick of the `built` variant merges, but the app picture
stands only as a placeholder for its state. Merge already took it (`undesigned-sketch.spec` "declares the state ...");
nothing refused it.

- The marker is the part file itself: the merged wrapper imports `./<state>.built` (`builtPictureModuleOf` in
  `sketch/part-definition.ts`, used by the wrapper). `builtPlaceholdersOf` reads those imports, `read-open-points.ts`
  passes them as `placeholders`, and `openPointsOf` adds one open point `redraw` per state:
  `<part>: ...; state <state> shows the app picture as a placeholder - redraw it in a sketch`. Any open point blocks
  build-ready, so the part stays not ready for it. A merged sketch whose part file no longer imports the picture clears
  it; the orphaned `<state>.built.ts` stays and counts for nothing.
- `redraw` is not in `SKETCH_KINDS`: the `built` variant itself would add it and `sketch ready` would refuse it.
- Studio lists it in the grid group as "Bild der App als Platzhalter - im Sketch neu zeichnen" with the state.

## As built (B251 data states)

Decision (grill, applies B251, ADR 0048): a part with `data: 'list'` names its data states in an explicit map; the word
match on state names no longer applies to a part with the map.

- `Part` takes `dataStates: { loading, error, empty }` (`PartDataStates`), each the name of the state that draws it;
  the type makes it required with `data: 'list'` (union `PartData`). The `DATA-STATES` rule rejects a part file with
  `data: 'list'` and no literal map of all three (`dataStatesOf` in `sketch/part-definition.ts`).
- `read-open-points.ts` passes the map; `openPointsOf` then asks for each mapped name the part does not draw, with the
  name in the line: `data part without the states error (listing-failed), empty (no-sketches)`. Without a map the word
  match stays (parts that load data).
- pages/sketches maps loading `comparing`, error `listing-failed`, empty `no-sketches`; the last two are not drawn, so
  B314 shows as an open point until they are. `real-open-points` budget: pages/sketches missing-state 1 -> 2.
- Verified: specs red first (open-points, part-definition, part-builder, rules/data-states); `vitest related` (cli 220
  files), cli typecheck and lint, `design check --part pages/sketches` on the working tree (0 findings, the two points).
- Not verified: Studio shows the mapped state name (it labels by `data` only and ignores `state`).
- Follow-up (grill): error maps to the drawn `list-error`, not a new `listing-failed`; a drawn state is not a missing
  one. B314 closed; its interim half needs no pick, the drawn list-error is the design. Budget pages/sketches
  missing-state back to 1 (empty `no-sketches`). The Studio line shows the mapped name: `empty (no-sketches)`.
  CLASS-UNDEFINED read the `dataStates` values as classes (`list-error` parses as a `list-*` utility); it skips them now.

## As built (B59 rest)

- `PartImplemented.app` is required; `readImplemented` reads a record without `app` as no record, and
  `readLegacyImplemented` returns it, so `design check` (`upgradeLegacyMarksOf`) adds `app` while its design hash
  holds and drops it otherwise. `markImplemented` takes `app` as a required option. Every studio entry already had
  `app` (16 of 16), so no record changed.
- `implemented-proof.ts` (`implementedRefusalsOf`) runs in `task --verify` before compare, and in `compare --affected`
  before it records a part again. It refuses `NO-SPEC` (no `*.spec.ts` in the component folder imports the component
  class and calls `createComponent(`), `FIXTURE-SPEC` (every test, or a `beforeEach`, uses a value imported from a
  `sample`/`fixture` module, from `.ethlete/`, or named `*_SAMPLE`/`*_FIXTURE`), and `LITERAL-TEXT` (a text node, a
  literal part of an interpolation, or a `title`/`alt`/`placeholder`/`aria-*` value with a letter, also a string literal
  such a binding can show through `?:`, `+`, `??`, `||`). It reads the templates of the component and of the component
  files in its folder that it reaches.
- Label map: no product names one, and the rule needs none. Literal text is refused, any binding passes, so each
  product reads its texts from whatever map it keeps (Studio: `STUDIO_LABELS`). A config key naming the map would only
  add a check that the binding reads from it.
- Existing records: the refusals over all 16 studio entries (no other product has an `implemented.json`) hit 7
  parts, listed in STATUS B59. They keep their records; the hits are fixed in the app, not exempted. `compare
--affected` cannot record them again until then.

## As built (B168 platform measures)

Findings 243 and 247. A part declares the native measures it imitates in `definePart({ platformMeasures })`: platform,
states, target selector, `width`/`height`, `inset` against an `edge` selector, and `ink` (glyph ink box), with a
`tolerance` of 0.5 px by default. The render check (`system/platform-measures.ts`, wired into `render-check.ts`) measures
them in Chromium per declared state: boxes via `getBoundingClientRect`, ink as the bounding box of the pixels in a shot of
the target that differ from its most frequent colour by at least half of the strongest difference. A miss is a
`PLATFORM-MEASURE` problem naming declared and measured values. The studio title bar declares the Windows 11 caption
buttons for `windows` and `windows-update`: 46 x 32 px tiles, top inset 0, close right inset 0, glyph ink 10 x 10 px
(minimize 10 x 1 px).

Verified: `platform-measures.spec.ts` in real Chromium goes red for a 10 px icon box with a padded viewBox (ink 6-7 px)
and for a 40 px tile, green for 10 px ink in a 46 px flush tile. `et design check --product studio --part
components/title-bar --working-tree` passes; with every declared value set wrong it fails with 6 `PLATFORM-MEASURE`
lines measuring 46 x 32 px tiles, insets 0 (close right 0), ink 10 x 10 px (minimize 10 x 1 px). Measured ink is whole
pixels at device scale 1, so the default 0.5 px tolerance holds. Not verified: the native Windows 11 original itself (the
declared numbers come from the finding, not from a shot of Windows); measures at a device scale other than 1. No
existing part declares measures, so the rule needs no ADR 0201 baseline.

worker) and the Studio build (async); each worker runs its design server and the fixture listing during the build, then
awaits the `built` message before warm-up and its first `next`, so no case starts before the build ends. The design

Moved from design-to-code.md line 1693: As built (667 a, shared in-flight draw): before a design server draws a key that is not in

As built (667 a, shared in-flight draw): before a design server draws a key that is not in the shared store, it takes
a lock file `draw.lock` in the key's store folder (`open` with `wx`, holding pid, start time and a token). A server that
finds the lock taken does not draw; it polls every 100 ms for the stored picture. It reads the picture only when the
read-files fingerprint matches its own checkout; else it draws itself once the lock is released. The owner releases the
lock after the store write, and also when the draw fails or is dropped, so a waiter then draws itself. A lock of a dead
pid, or one older than the draw limit (`DRAW_LIMIT_MS` 60 s, scaled by load), is taken over, and the waiter logs
"past the draw limit" when the age was the reason. Fresh draws neither lock nor wait. The ledger counts `waitedTotal`
next to `drawnTotal` (`/__design/queue`); the e2e `ready` line and each case line print both.
Bite, unit: two stores on one folder, the second waits and reads the first's picture; two shooters, the second draws 0
and waits for 1; a dead-pid lock and an old lock are taken over; a failed draw and a changed input file let the waiter
draw. `spec:stress` 4/4 on the three touched specs. E2E, 7 first-load and Fit cases, 3 workers, cold store each run,
load 4 to 28: setup draws per worker HEAD 22/22/22 (66) and new 21+1/13+6/12+2 waited (46 drawn, 9 waited). Plain
7/7, 115.2 s HEAD vs 112.8 s new. With `--hold-listings 14000`: setup HEAD 20/21/22 (63), new 46 drawn and 9 waited
as above; 7/7, 226.3 s HEAD vs 220.4 s new. Case draws hardly changed (25 to 55 per Fit case, 3 waited for in all):
each case runs another target on another worker, so the workers rarely draw the same key at once. Not explained: the
held Wide Fit case drew 79 at HEAD and 132 new, with 0 waited for in it; one run each. No
"past the draw limit" line in the runs. About 12 setup draws per worker stay: the fixture compare draws fresh on
purpose. Suspect: a lock is taken when the draw is queued, not when it starts, so a waiter may wait for a draw that
sits in the owner's backlog; bounded by the draw limit, not seen in the runs. A server that is killed leaves its locks
(2 left after a plain run); the next waiter takes them over and the store sweep removes dead-pid locks. Not verified: a
full `yarn studio:e2e`, CI, more than 3 workers, a waiter that really reaches the draw limit.

`node_modules/.design-explore`. Correction: the old name was `shots-<10 hex>` (`viteCacheOf` cuts the sha1 to 10), not
the full sha1. Only directories that match `^shots-[0-9a-f]{10}$` go; `part-shots`, `shots-foo`, `vite-*` and every other
name stay. It runs once per start in `serveDesign`, under the same condition that turns on the shot store, and is not
awaited, so the start is not slower; a failed removal logs one line and the server goes on. Bite: spec

from launch including the boot. Not verified: a spec for the `serve.ts` wiring, several servers that start at once,

973 as built: `tools/scripts/nx-heavy-wait.mjs` is a local Nx plugin in `nx.json` whose `preTasksExecution` calls
`waitForNoHeavyRun('nx')`, so a direct `npx nx ...` waits while push:suite or studio:e2e holds the heavy run lock. Probe
(Nx 24.0.2, `cli:lint` in a scratch copy): Cause: with the daemon off the hook runs in a plugin worker the CLI spawns,
sees the caller's `ETHLETE_HEAVY_RUN_HELD`, and its stderr reaches the caller. Cause: with the daemon on it runs in a
worker under the daemon that gets the caller's env per call (held `222`, `333`, then unset, each seen), but its stderr
goes to the daemon log, and Nx does not forward `TMPDIR`: the daemon's `os.tmpdir()` is `/tmp`, the callers' lock is in
the macOS per-user temp dir, so the first daemon-on refusal check ran the task. `lockFileOf` reads that dir with
`getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR` when `TMPDIR` is unset; after it the daemon-on check refuses too. Cause: the worker
cannot exit the CLI with 2 (`process.exit(2)` reads "Plugin worker exited unexpectedly", exit 1), so the hook throws the
heavy-gate line instead: one `NX nx: heavy run lock held by ...; run again after it ends` line, exit 1. Cause: Nx fails
an isolated plugin call after 10 min, so the hook waits at most 9 min, then refuses. A lock-holder child, no lock or a
dead holder return at once; `ETHLETE_HEAVY_NO_WAIT=1` refuses at once. Exempt with `ETHLETE_HEAVY_EXEMPT=design`: `yarn
design`, `yarn design:check` and the cli/app builds of `studio-code.mjs` (et:design, studio app serve). Added time on a
cached no-lock `cli:lint`: about 450 ms daemon off (1.83 s to 2.28 s), 200-900 ms daemon on, nearly all of it the worker
start. Spec: `nx-heavy-wait.spec.mjs`; without the exempt check, the env handoff, the holder check or the no-wait flag,
or with `lockFileOf` ignoring the daemon case, a case fails. Suspect: two daemon callers at once share the worker's env,
so one may see the other's held or exempt flag.

`merge-remedies.spec.ts` (not ready; no pick; rejected pick - reopen; no baseline - rebase; changed part - port and
rebase; uncommitted drawn-on part - commit; uncommitted edits in the way - revert, or commit then rebase; product not
in the committed config.json - commit it; another part imports @shared/ - move the code in; the three `mergeStepOf`
refusals), `merge-shared.spec.ts` (orphan shared/ file - delete it; target's own shared/ folder - rename it),
`design-lint.spec.ts` (new lint warnings - fix them). Through the API, rejecting the picked variant drops the pick, so
the "rejected - reopen it first" refusal only meets a sketch file that holds both; the spec builds that state.

Cause (bite in `sketch-base-stale-remedy.spec.ts`): a sketch drawn while its own part had an uncommitted change
records a baseline no commit holds; SKETCH-BASE-STALE names `sketch rebase`, `portBaseChanges` refuses "no commit holds
the state the baseline recorded, port it by hand", and the refusal said "then run sketch rebase again", so following it
ran the same rebase three times with the same refusal. Only `--ported` clears it. The refusal now names the full
`sketch rebase <target> --ported --product <name> --by <model id>` command; the spec follows the printed remedies, clears
SKETCH-BASE-STALE, and merges after the part is committed. Not verified: the "built-in base - --override" refusal has
no spec (the fixture has no built-in base).

### As built: 977

Cause: a refused `merge --allowed-by` kept its agent pick in `sketch.json`; a later `--variant b` merged the stale `a`.
Now a refused allowed merge and the `mergeStepOf` pre-check restore the sketch, and a pick by a model id counts as no
pick. Verified: three biting specs, related specs, lint, typecheck. Not verified: a live run; a non-model-id `--by`.

B220b follow-up as built (2026-11-14): on top of fa26a43d5 and bf732f7d1, a sketch merge (CLI, Studio, auto-merge) rebases the other stale sketches inside its journaled step, before its commit, and the merge commit holds what the rebase wrote (`commitMergeResultSync` `sketchDirs`, the folders `rebaseStaleSketches` wrote: rebased or marked `portAfterMerge`). The post-commit hook runs `sketch rebase-open --json` and commits the rebase by path as `fix(repo): Rebase the sketches <sha> made stale`; a conflict's `portAfterMerge` mark is committed too, a file already dirty before the rebase is left out and named. SKETCH-BASE-STALE in `design check` stays: it is the gate for a conflict or a stale base from an uncommitted edit, which no commit rebases. Verified: after-merge spec (merge commit leaves the checkout clean; red without `sketchDirs`), hook spec, vitest related (143 files), live hook in a git-initialised scratch copy with all hooks: title-bar edit -> 4 sketches rebased and committed, clean tree, about 5 s for both commits. Not live: a Studio merge end to end.

Sketch switch fast path as built (2026-11-14): `sketchRead$` takes `picks` (the picked entry as an observable); a sketch picked after Studio start is compared alone with `&sketch=<target>` while the full listing runs, cut off once the full listing answers. Before, a switch waited for the full listing. Measured in a scratch copy, Studio booted on `pages/system`, click on `system@canvas-note` once its tree row shows, time to the first `[data-sk-changed="true"]` cell, cold design server per run, before and after alternated: before 8.4/4.9/8.4 s (median 8.4 s; an earlier before-only set 9.6/5.3/5.6 s), after 3.9/3.7/3.8 s (median 3.8 s). Verified: sketch-read spec for a later pick (hangs without the fix), vitest related, live shot of the switched sketch with its changed pictures. Not verified: a switch to a second sketch while the first switched compare still runs.

B514 as built (2026-11-15): Cause (probe): the compare case "no state is marked before the compare answers" unrouted
its page route while a second held listing handler was still in flight; Playwright then continues that route
server-side, and the handler's late `route.fulfill` threw `Route is already handled!` into the next case on the worker.
A standalone Playwright probe shows the throw without draining and none with it. The case now switches its handler to
`route.fallback()`, awaits the in-flight handlers, then unroutes. Verified: the probe; both cases locally (6/6, one
worker). Not verified: the exact CI order (compare case directly before the frame case) did not occur locally.
